Many, many years ago, before Phainon was Phainon, before his heart knew pain and his body knew strife, he was still not an ordinary boy.

His golden blood, of course, was one thing, and that was of great interest to the town elders, but that was not what endeared him to the other townsfolk. The fact that he was an alpha was far more interesting to them.

Aedes Elysiae did not have many alphas, or omegas for that matter. Nobody knew the reason, and nobody bothered to find it. They were simply a village of betas, no need to waste any time pondering the matter beyond that.

But then, Phainon was born, an alpha in a long line of betas. A surprise, to be certain.

His mother recounted the tale of his birth to him once, how the midwife had gone ghostly white when trying to determine his sex, thinking that he had some sort of physical malady, before she managed to piece things together, and had told his mother, with apologetic relief, that she had a healthy alpha boy, to both of his parents' shock.

The midwife was not the only one unaccustomed to encountering alphas. The town's doctor had only a faint understanding of how to support his secondary sexual health, offering only a book titled Alpha Physiology that was so old the back cover had fallen off. It wasn't a riveting read for a teenager who'd just reached the age of his first rut, and he'd awkwardly returned it after it failed to help him in any way.

And the other townsfolk--well, they had all sorts of strange advice for him, none of it impactful. They certainly knew nothing of alphas themselves, so despite their fascination in him, they couldn't offer him much. He eventually stopped paying attention to what they had to say, and he tried to figure things out for himself, which also didn't get him anywhere.

It was a shame, since his parents didn't know what to do about his ruts either. They tried to find some way to help ease them, but the concoctions of healing herbs they would prepare for him didn't do a thing, as the recipes were mostly archaic nonsense. After a few failed attempts, they decided they'd just give him cold compresses to help with the fever and some painkillers for the aches that would spring up. It was better than nothing, but not good.

Phainon wasn't violent during his ruts--far from it, in fact. He would lay listless in bed, body burning up, mind a slow, sludgy mess for the better part of a week, and then, when his senses cleared up, he'd go right back to his ordinary life. Besides that interruption every three months, Phainon scarcely thought about his secondary gender.

He'd reckon that's why he's never been a proper alpha, at least compared to what Okhemans think he should be. Whatever natural instincts he's meant to have are lacking. All of that drivel about how he's meant to view omegas as conquests or prizes and should covet power and fame has always seemed foreign to him. He'd reckon that such behavior isn't really natural at all, and it's all due to nurture, not nature.

Well, that was what he thought until today, anyway. It seems some of those urges have decided to rear their ugly heads.

Dear Titans above, he thinks he's losing his mind. The moment he walked into the meeting and saw Mydei, smelled Mydei, he wasn't able to focus on anything but him. He's had multiple quints to piece himself back together and it's only getting worse the longer he thinks about it.

What about his scent has changed? He still can't name it, all he can recognize is that it has changed further, becoming even richer, even deeper, even more intoxicating. During that stupid meeting, the urge to clamber over the table and bury his nose in the crook of Mydei's neck was near overwhelming.

And it wasn't just the scent, either. Phainon tried his best to stare at him discretely, and Mydei seemed so much softer. Such a descriptor is so foreign to him that it almost feels wrong, but it's the only one that comes to mind. All of the sharpness of his well-toned body was muted, rounded at the edges, gentle where it was once imposing--at least from what he could see. Mydei's not been wearing his rather revealing outfit since his return, he's taken to hiding his wonderful physique under a rotating cast of conservative chitons and even a himation that Phainon wasn't aware he owned.

Does he know the reason for any of this? Certainly not. In the end, all of this contemplation has led him to a single conclusion: he wants Mydei.

Now that he's alone once more, that desire has only become more potent. He's spent the better half of curtain-fall hour pacing a hole in his carpet, a low growl thrumming in his chest, jaw clenched tight in agony.

He wants Mydei here, wants to touch him all over, wants to sink his teeth into his waiting flesh, wants to drown in that delectable scent until it's a part of him, wants to--

"Quit being ridiculous," he scolds himself, hoping the sound of his own voice will ground him. It does not. Nothing seems to help this overwhelming restlessness, and his thoughts have only grown more tempestuous.

What he really needs is some fresh air, he thinks, though he's not keen on leaving the safe comfort of his chambers. Another minute of pacing later, and he decides he'll risk it. He worries he'll lose his wits if he has to stay here any longer. It's curtain-fall hour anyway, he should be afforded some privacy. Nobody will witness him in the throes of this breakdown.

But after mustering up the courage to step outside, he only makes it a few paces before he's stopped dead in his tracks by a rather unexpected sight. It's Lady Hyacine, a large basket cradled in her arms, walking down the hallway with her back to him.

She may be a Chrysos Heir, and she may come to Okhema for frequent visits, but she doesn't live in the Mamoreal Palace like his peers. As far as he knows, she doesn't have any reason to be milling about here. He thought she would've returned to the Grove already--he's relatively certain that Anaxa did, he's not sure why she wouldn't join him.

Even stranger than all of that is the fact that she stops in front of the doors to Mydei's chambers. Why is a doctor seeing Mydei?

His mind races, considering every possibility for why she's visiting him. Is she delivering his next dose of suppressants? Since they both use medication to halt their cycles, Phainon never really paid attention to the schedule of Mydei's heats, though he should be due for one quite soon, if memory serves. But suppressants don't need to be delivered in such a large basket, it's just a little case of pills.

Perhaps she has some other medicine for him? He looked--rather inexplicably--unwell during the meeting, so unwell that Anaxa insisted she check on him when he ran off suddenly and failed to return. But what sort of medicine would Mydei need? Unless the nature of his immortality has suddenly changed, he shouldn't be getting sick. Though, there was an instance when he got cursed by an old artifact they stumbled across a few years back--perhaps something similar happened on this mission? It could explain a few things.

And then, the more irrational thoughts flood in, brought upon by some part of his alpha hindbrain that has suddenly become quite overactive.

Does she desire him? Is she courting him? Does she think she has a chance to rival Phainon's affections?

Truly ridiculous things for him to think, and yet, he thinks them anyway. He's not sure why he's suddenly become so territorial. Mydei is free to do what he wishes, far be it from Phainon to try to dictate the life of a man who could end his own in a heartbeat. Of course, letting himself be courted by Hyacine isn't one of the things he'd entertain, and Hyacine herself wouldn't dream of such grossly unprofessional behavior.

But even so, all of that logical thinking can't counter the jealousy snared in his heart or soothe his racing mind.

What's wrong with him?

He practically sprints down the hallway before Hyacine can reappear, desperate for escape from her, from Mydei, from everything. His legs pump underneath him, thoughtlessly carrying him through the palace until he's finally made it outside, to a mercifully empty balcony.

Kephale's light is a smidge dimmer at this late hour, enough to cast the city before him in a gentler light. The view is always majestic from the palace, as the high vantage point lets one see the tops of the grandest temples and the low, sloping hills packed with quaint homes.

He braces himself against the balcony railing, panting despite the lack of exertion, eyes burning as he stares out at the vast sky. His fingers dig into the marble hard enough to ache. He forces himself to breathe, each shuddering inhale feeling like he's forcing water into his lungs instead of air.

Slowly, his body stills. The commotion within him quiets to a simmer, leaving confusion in its wake.

Nothing about any of this makes a lick of sense.

Mydei isn't the avoidant type--far from it, really. When he has issues, he works them out immediately. So, why is he so determinedly avoiding just Phainon and nobody else?

At this point, he's fed up with all of it. He's been a mess for weeks; if he doesn't pull it together soon, he can only imagine how cross Aglaea will become as his performance suffers, and how many people might suffer in turn.

How will he fix this?

It seems impossible when everything's already in shambles. Hoping for a solution may be foolish--or perhaps not. All he needs to do is quit wallowing in the shame of his mistakes and look at this with a clear head.

What did he do to Mydei to prompt this in the first place? He doesn't know. He still doesn't think he's done anything wrong. So, he'll do exactly what's worked in the past when he's had questions: ask Mydei directly.

It's been exceedingly difficult to catch him at an opportune moment, but with some determination, Phainon's sure he can get him in the right setting for a conversation. He'll be blunt, in the exact manner that Mydei appreciates, and he'll get his answer. Whatever worries he has will be properly assuaged, Phainon will make sure of it.

By the gods, he swears going to get this all worked out--he's not going to fail again.

Two days later, Phainon marches over to knock on Mydei's door, and receives no response.

He'd hoped that waiting to talk to him would've increased the likelihood that he'd be in a better mood, but his patience is meaningless if he can't even find him. Still determined, he prepares himself for another hunt across the city.

Unfortunately, searching his usual haunts, once again, leads him nowhere, and unlike before, he doesn't stumble across him at the market in a stroke of luck. Lacking any other guesses, he contemplates the matter for a while, and finally decides to go to one of the people who knows Mydei best.

"Lord Krateros, good morning!" Phainon cheerily greets, giving the man a smile he's sure could melt even the coldest of hearts.

Krateros is, as always, completely immune to his charms, and he barely acknowledges his presence, only offering a grunt as he continues to polish his blade. He's definitely not allowed to have a sword unsheathed in the Mamoreal Palace, but he's never minded the rules in the past, and Phainon certainly isn't going to report him for disorderly conduct.

"Can I ask you a question?" he says, after a beat of awkward silence passes.

"You already did. If you have something to say, boy, then say it."

"I was just wondering if you'd seen Mydei today, or if he told you where he might be at this hour."

Krateros finally bothers to look at Phainon, his stern expression morphing into thinly veiled concern, and gods, is that the last emotion one would ever want to see him express.

"I don't know. He promised to meet with me two days ago to discuss some matters regarding the Kremnoan detachment, but he never showed. I figured he was off gallivanting with you, wasting his time."

Phainon would be offended if the sickly twist of dread brewing within him wasn't so prevalent. As it is, his focus isn't directed at the slight against him.

"He'd never miss a meeting with you."

"Which is exactly the problem," Krateros huffs, "and he's not responding to my messages, either."

"Umm... Well, in that case... I'll try asking around some more. Thank you, regardless."

Krateros's words are troubling, to say the least. Phainon's selfish motivations to find Mydei have suddenly become much less selfish, if the Kremnoan's crown prince really is missing. Avoiding Phainon is one matter, but to avoid his own people--well, that goes from strange to something else entirely.

It's surely fine, just a misunderstanding, he tells himself, trying to keep the panic at bay with middling success. It's all he can do to not sprint to Aglaea and beg her to find Mydei--she won't obey his whims, he's already well aware.

The Tribios, however, might help him, so he hurries over to the Garden of Life, correctly assuming that he'll find them playing with the chimeras at this time. At entry hour, the gardens are sparsely populated, with only the keepers and a few scholars milling about, and the chimeras themselves have yet to start their work.

Tribbie is cooing over a little red one who seems to be new addition to the Garden, Trinnon is quietly stroking a black one resting peacefully on her lap, and Trianne is setting up what looks like a race with a few rambunctious ones, having them line up at the far end of the small courtyard.

It's pleasant. Familiar. The dread in Phainon's heart ebbs as he takes it all in, and he lets out an even, measured breath.

"Snowy!" Tribbie cries, before he has a chance to greet them all himself. She leaves her place by the chimera's side to flutter his way, one of her tiny hands waving enthusiastically.

He can't quite muster the same energy as her today, but still offers a wave in return. "Good morning, Lady Tribbie. I have a few questions for you if you're not too busy?"

"Of course we can answer... Oh, Snowy, is something troubling you? You look so sad..."

Though he's not told Tribbie most of his woes regarding Mydei--it feels a bit odd to discuss with her--she's noticed his low mood, and offered him consolation in that gentle manner of hers. Her sisters have given him support too, in their own unique ways. He always appreciates it, but this time, he'll need something a bit more substantial than candies or head pats.

"I am a bit troubled, unfortunately... Hopefully it'll all be resolved soon enough. I was wondering if Mydei's been sent on a mission? I can't seem to find him today, and he's not responding to my messages."

"Hmm... We don't think he's on a mission, no. Agy doesn't think he's ready to go on one yet, she wants him to rest more. We definitely didn't request for him to leave the city. There's nothing we need in Janusopolis for the moment, and we agree that he could use a break. He doesn't seem to be feeling the best."

"So, you don't know where he might be?"

She shakes her head resolutely. "We're sorry, Snowy. There's not much we can do... We can try sending him a message if you'd like!"

"It's worth a shot," he replies, shrugging. If he's not responding to Krateros, he's not sure why'd he'd respond to Tribbie, but it's better to cover all of one's bases.

Twenty minutes later, with no response to be had, Phainon's about ready to continue his search elsewhere when a somewhat unexpected visitor gracefully makes her way into the courtyard.

"There you are, Cas!"

Apparently, the Tribios were expecting to see Castorice here. They crowd around her--or crowd as close as they're able. Phainon makes his way over to find that she's carrying a large bag in hand, which he recognizes as the one that holds all her crafting supplies. It's easy to guess what they're planning to do together.

"Greetings, I brought the right hooks this time... Oh, Lord Phainon," she says, noticing his approach. "I was going to teach the Ladies Tribios how to crochet. Are you here to join in?"

"I don't think I'm cut out for crocheting, and I'm short on time, anyway. I'm currently on a hunt for... Hold on, can I ask if you've seen Mydei anywhere since the day before yesterday?"

The abrupt question gives Castorice some pause. "Have I seen him? I don't recall... Is there a reason you're asking?"

"I'm trying to find him. Nobody's heard from him since the meeting with the Grove."

"A few days ago..." she muses, eyes closed in contemplation. Phainon expects another dead end, but then, she perks back up with a quiet aha.

"I did see him on a side street near one of the city walls on the night of the meeting, though I'm not sure where he was going. He seemed to be in a hurry... I couldn't determine anything else, I only saw him briefly at a distance. I'm aware that's not very helpful, my apologies."

"It's very helpful," he assures her, "I'll go check the area you saw him if you'd put it in my teleslate."

With a location marked down to check and his spirits lifted, Phainon rushes out of the palace with a hurried goodbye to the others. Now that he has an actual lead, he's certain to find Mydei soon.

He hopes so, anyway. His hopes are dashed after he spends far too much time milling around in the side street of note, finding it to be completely ordinary and not at all helpful. It's in the Kremnoan District, which seemed promising at first, but clearly, Mydei must've just been passing through, and his destination wasn't in the area.

After asking every nearby Kremnoan if they've seen their prince and crawling around like an idiot on the ground searching for clues, he leans against the closest wall with a sigh, feeling the energy ebbing from him.

He's defeated. Trying to find one man in the sprawling city of Okhema, even one as notable as Mydei, is like finding a needle in a haystack. Giving up sounds more unpleasant than continuing his search, but perhaps he should take a break.

"Hey, golden boy, pick your head up!"

Or not. Of course, his most devoted tormentor is here at another one of his lowest moments. She waltzes up to him with all her usual swagger, tail swishing and hips swaying, with a balance coin dancing across her fingers.

"... Cipher, I'm not in the mood for this right now."

"I'm giving you encouragement, but alright, if that's how you're gonna be, suit yourself," she scoffs, before tossing the coin into subspace.

"I don't feel encouraged. It's just... ugh, you don't even come to Okhema that frequently, and you're choosing to bother me while I'm busy instead of doing... whatever it is that you do," he mutters. It's a bit rude, and yet, he can't find it in him to play nice. He already knows she won't care if he's snappish.

"I've got very important business, but right now, I'm here to help you!"

Her words alone are enough to make him recoil. The wide grin on her face doesn't make it any less unnerving.

"You're going to help me? What sort of extortion is this?"

She waves a hand dismissively. "Oh, I already got paid. Princess Homebody begged me to help you, she sent me this long, heartfelt message about how she's so worried, and you've been such a mess lately... I didn't read the whole thing, I dunno all the details. But she promised to make an adorable crochet doll of yours truly if I did you a quick favor, and that's a deal I couldn't refuse!"

He's not sure if he should feel touched that Castorice was so worried about him, or disconcerted that she turned to Cipher for aid before anybody else. Right now, Cipher doesn't seem particularly nefarious, no more than usual, anyway, so he supposes he appreciates it.

"That's surprisingly considerate of you."

"I know, right?" she preens. "But enough about that, what sort of favor do you want from me? It has to be quick, like less than three minutes kind of quick, or I'm going to ask for more payment."

He's not exactly sure what sort of favor Castorice expected from her, but Phainon knows exactly what he'd like. "Could you do a lap through the city and find Mydei for me? Just tell me his exact location, that's all I want."

"You want me to stalk your boytoy? That's kinda weird, honestly... I've got a lax moral code, but this goes against it, buddy--"

"I'm not stalking him, I'm trying to find him so I can talk to him! He's not responding to anybody's messages and I'm getting worried."

"Oh, so he's just playing hard to get. If it'll make you feel better, then fine, I'll track him down. I'll be back!"

She's gone in a flash--but she doesn't return as quickly as he expected. Two minutes later--which is an eternity for her standards--she blinks back into existence in front of him, a new furrow to her brow.

"Huh. I couldn't find him anywhere."

"... What do you mean?"

"I mean I couldn't find him. I don't think I can put it in simpler terms for you."

Phainon's legs give out underneath him. The wall behind him is his only support as he sinks to the ground.

Cipher makes a muted exclamation that he can't quite hear past the ringing in his ears. Her face seems to waver before him as she bends down and starts vigorously shaking his shoulder.

"--non, Phainon! What the hell? Do I need to call the doctor or something?"

"He's missing, Cipher."

"Mydei's missing? I wouldn't say that, he's just not in the city. I mean, that little prince goes on mission all the time, he must be off on one right now, yeah? Go ask the Goldweaver if you must, I'm sure she knows. There's no need to freak out."

"But he's not--" he stops himself immediately, not wanting to raise his voice. He forces himself to take the deepest inhale he can manage, lets it out slowly, and then pulls himself back upright.

There's no need to freak out, as Cipher put it. That won't help anything. What he needs to do is ask Aglaea.

"Lady Aglaea, greetings."

Aglaea does not react to Phainon's approach, but when he speaks, she dips her head in silent greeting. She's not in the baths as she'd usually be at this hour, instead seated at one of the palace's circular dining tables, a pot of tea forgotten before her. She's not relaxing either, she's checking the golden threads; her hands are raised, and he can see the faint, thin sheen of them glimmering betwixt her splayed fingers.

He's not sure if she's doing a regular survey or if she's actively searching for something, but whatever the case may be, he feels a twinge of guilt for interrupting her work. Perhaps she senses his hesitation, as she lowers her hands to rest in her lap, and gives him her full attention.

"Yes, Lord Phainon?"

Suddenly, he's not quite sure what to say. "Umm... I was just... I was wondering if you could, uh, check the threads for me? I know you don't like to do it for no reason, and you said you wouldn't do it last time I asked--I'm sorry if it's a bother, but I'm really worried this time. I can't find Mydei again, and he's not answering anybody's messages--not mine, not the Tribios, not Krateros--"

Aglaea clears her throat sharply, cutting him off. "Calm yourself. I can sense your anxiety, and I understand your concern. However, it is also unnecessary. I was just checking for Lord Mydei's presence myself, as I've also noticed his absence.

"He is not in Okhema, and I cannot locate him. It appears he has gone missing, and likely has been since our meeting with the Grove."

Her tone is even as she delivers the news. Not impassive, but careful. She knows it's an issue, and yet, she's still planning how to act. This is how she's always been since the day Phainon first stumbled into Okhema, skin streaked with ichor and psyche nearly broken, and she took him under her wing. If she weren't so prudent, she wouldn't have made it all these hundreds of years.

She's imparted the same nature onto him as she's helped guide him toward his destined future as their leader. It's what is best for both him and the future of Amphoreus. The Flamechase needs sagacity and care. If his emotions get the best of him, he'll make mistakes in his haste to act, and he may just ruin a millennium of effort.

Years of training, of affirmation, of honing--he has been tempered to a perfect, controlled edge.

But the confirmation does not affect Phainon in the way he'd imagine, and any control he has left over his mind has snapped.

All of his earlier dread remains at a simmer. His breathing is even, his body stays upright, his strength does not wane. Instead, he begins to feel anger, a great wave of anger that wells up steadily, mounting, burning fiercely within his chest. It turns his blood to fire and his will to iron.

If Mydei has gone missing, then somebody must be at fault. Somebody's done something to him--perhaps even hurt him.

And he is going to return that hurt tenfold.

He's walking away from Aglaea without a farewell, ignoring whatever she says in his wake. She cannot stop him. If she's disappointed in what he's about to do, he doesn't have the hindsight to regret it.

Only one thing matters in this moment.

He's always known who might dare to hurt Mydei. Those Council bastards--they've always hated him. He's a foreign prince of a once-rival nation who controls a considerable faction in their city, and whose power as a Chrysos Heir oppresses their own. Aglaea may be the main target of their ire, but he's next in line.

And right now, he's vulnerable. He's returned from a difficult expedition that failed to bear fruit, one that the Council has vocally opposed as a waste of the city's resources.

Of course they chose to strike now.

A sliver of restraint is what keeps Phainon from charging into the Dawncloud with his broadsword drawn. He forces himself to walk slowly, with measured strides. His expression is neutral, revealing nothing of his intentions. But even so, he knows his countenance radiates with his anger, so great is its power. The aides in his path flee. Council members cower. Civilians stare, transfixed.

Let them watch, he thinks. The world can know of his devotion, it matters not.

Elder Caenis is certainly about to know of its force.

She's talking with a few of her lackeys, smiling without warmth, acting as if she hasn't done anything. Phainon approaches without a moment of hesitation. He's not going to tread on eggshells; if they won't play nice, he has no reason to keep up the veneer of peace.

Perhaps the force of his glare is enough to make her turn his way before he can say anything. She seems mildly surprised and, as always, displeased, but she cools her expression before speaking.

"Oh my, what brings a Chrysos Heir to my doorstep without invitation? Do you require the Council's aid?"

"Certainly not," he spits. "You know why I'm here."

"I don't, actually. I believe our relationship is rather amicable at the moment, I cannot understand this sudden ire."

"What did you do to Mydei?"

"What did I do to Mydei? I did nothing but send a new draft of the Okheman-Kremnoan peace treaty for him to look over. It's very important to us both, as his people have many demands that we try to accomodate--"

"I don't care about your terrible attempts at diplomacy," he interrupts, "and your lies disgust me. I'm going to ask you again: what did you do to Mydei?"

"You seem to think I have a reason to... harm him, or whatever it is that you're insinuating, and I fail to grasp why you'd accuse me of something so utterly ridiculous--and so unsubstantiated."

Caenis has the gall to feign confusion. Phainon grates his back teeth together in a desperate attempt to redirect the tension in his body. One more lie from her mouth, and he's going to close the distance between them, wrap his hands around her neck, and send her right to the gates of the Netherworld.

She deserves it, not just for this, but for all the harm she's done in Okhema. Her ploys to cling to power, to oppose progress with all the willpower left in her hate-riddled, decrepit body, to hinder the Flamechase for no real reason; if she were gone, and the Council were dissolved, their entire world would be much better off.

It would be so easy. There's nobody around besides a few spectators. The nearest guards are at least a fifteen second sprint away, which is more than enough time to wring her neck until the bones are nothing but shattered fragments under crushed muscle--

And then, the air around him constricts.

The feeling is not quite familiar, but he recognizes the source regardless: Aglaea's threads. He's seen her use them for more than just communication; they are insidiously lethal when she desires to fight, garroting Titankin and Tide-corrupted beasts with ease.

Now, they tighten without ensnaring him, acting as a slap upon the wrist with the looming threat of something much more terrible should he take another step forward. After all, she can sense his intentions, and can read the darkness dredged up from deep within his mind that just threatened to show itself; she knows exactly what he was poised to do.

He's frozen.

As he listens to the sound of approaching footsteps, he dares not turn to face the woman he knows is behind him. It isn't out of defiance. His violent fantasy has vanished, and in the aftermath, he's shocked at himself.

"Elder Caenis speaks the truth. The Council has nothing to do with Mydei's disappearance," Aglaea says without greeting, tone steely.

Her words linger. Nobody speaks, not even Caenis, who looks at Phainon with undisguised anger. At this moment, he feels he deserves her wrath.

He was about to doom them all, and for what reason, but an unsubstantiated accusation against her because he wanted somebody to blame, some outlet for his instinct-driven anger that was too potent for him to handle on his own. It's incredibly foolish--and confounding. He cared deeply for Mydei, but not in the manner that he'd act so irrationally for his sake.

What's gotten into him?

Once it's clear that he isn't going to try anything, the threads fall away, and in their place, Aglaea's hand rests lightly upon his shoulder, perhaps attempting to ground him. It helps, somewhat.

"I must apologize for Lord Phainon's actions. He's currently unwell, and isn't in his right mind. I assure you, this will not happen again."

"If it does, be aware that I will not hesitate to take significant action against him and your little Flamechase. Now, I believe you've long overstayed your welcome in the Dawncloud, Lord Phainon."

Her sneered words linger in his mind as Aglaea leads him away. He cannot muster up the strength to speak--doesn't know what he'd say if he could. Shame burns a hole in his chest. What he just did is unforgivable, and he knows Aglaea is disappointed, even as she brings him back to the tea table and pours him a cup of his own.

"... I know there is no apology for my actions. Bring whatever punishment you wish upon me," he murmurs, after emptying his cup. Its warmth doesn't do much to soothe him, but a facsimile of comfort is better than nothing at all.

"I'm not going to punish you."

He almost can't believe her, and yet, she has no reason to lie to him. For a moment, he's quiet, considering the weight of her forgiveness and wondering what he's done to deserve it.

"Why not?" he finally asks.

"It is as I said: you're currently unwell. The way you just acted was not natural to you, but instead driven by a hormonal response and made worse by your fraught emotional state. All of this became evident the moment I directly touched you with the threads.

"Additionally, considering the severe self-deprecation you're prone to exhibiting, I can only assume that such an incident will not occur again. No matter what I say, you will blame yourself entirely, and will close yourself off once more."

Her analyses of him are frequent enough for him to be resigned to them, and he can only sigh. "If something like that happens again, and you're not around to stop me, what might the outcome be?"

She contemplates his question as she tops up his cup. Frankly, he doesn't want to be here any longer, but he's not so foolish as to run from Aglaea. To believe he could in the first place would be a folly.

"Repression will only make matters worse," she finally says. "There is a time and a place for everything, including expressions of anger. Perhaps I can provide you with a suitable outlet by sending you out to search for Lord Mydei?"

Any protest immediately dies on his tongue, and he allows Aglaea to continue uninterrupted.

"Considering that he was in the city just two days prior, I cannot imagine that he's gone too far from Okhema. I'd recommend checking the refugee camps first, and then, if that proves unfruitful, you should move onto Janusopolis. I wish I could prove more specific instructions, but there are simply too many unknowns."

"That's enough to work with, thank you--and thank you for the opportunity as well. I know you don't want my apologies once more, but... I truly am sorry for my recent behavior."

Aglaea's lips tilt up into a slight smile. "I am aware that you care deeply for Lord Mydei, and I understand. I would be a poor bearer of my coreflame if I did not. It's evident that you've found great strength in your bond, and will achieve more yet. Love is a powerful force, one that will motivate you more than any other that could search for him."

"Of course. I'll bring him home, Lady Aglaea. You have my word."

chapters.html:
Before the Calamity war, before the Black Tide, and before the Titans abandoned their mortal charges, Amphoreus was a glorious world. No living soul can recall that time of boundless prosperity, but even in ruins, the remains of great city-states stand proud, a testament to what once was. One can easily imagine how they might look bathed in the light of Aquila's gaze, dotted across the vibrant, teeming canvas of grassy hills and limestone cliffs, overlooking the blue-green oceans of placid temperament, surrounded by fertile fields. What did it all seem to promise but peace everlasting, as none dared suggest the boons of their gods could be finite.

But they were, of course. That wellspring has dried, and the dreams of their world have long since withered into clinging buds of hope. Outside of the warm cradle of Kephale's embrace, Amphoreus is naught but a stark, cold wasteland.

Being stuck out in such unforgiving conditions only makes Mydei more eager to point out the Evernight's bounty of flaws. It's storming again, and he's watching it from the shelter he scrambled into when it first started pouring down.

Somehow, the sky darkens even further than before with the cloud cover; the lack of visibility is disconcerting. Though his body aches and his eyelids are drooping, he knows he cannot rest here. He remains vigilant, listening for the sounds of shifting Titankin amongst the pattering of raindrops on the wooden roof above him.

For those without a warrior's inclination, the plethora of monsters is an issue, but for Mydei, they're of little concern. In Janusopolis, at least, there's only Titankin, which are so easy to dispatch he'd wager he could very well do it in his sleep.

Of course, he won't risk it; regardless, there's multiple reasons he shouldn't rest, not here. Like most things in Janusopolis, this house is falling apart, and progressively more water is beginning to leak inside as the minutes pass. He can't imagine it'd be very comfortable to stay here for more than a quint.

At least he has a himation to cover himself, one sturdy enough to hold up to the weather. Ptolemy got it for him many years ago, and despite all Mydei has been through, the himation has remained intact, save for a few sewn-on patches. His friends would all be pleased to know the thing has lasted so long.

It hasn't gotten much use since those days in the detachment--not until he first started showing and realized he needed some way to conceal his body, that is. Now, it keeps him warm as he braves the wilds of Janusopolis.

He has more comforts in the safe room he cleared out, tucked deep within an old temple on the city's outskirts, but he hasn't been spending much time there. There's far too much to do outside of it. Countless Titankin populate this dead city, and he has made it his job to clear them out. Beyond completing his resolution, he'll bide his time, awaiting the day of his return.

When he first suspected his pregnancy, he was already quite certain of the circumstances of the child's conception, and meeting with Hyacine on the evening of his departure provided confirmation.

It was an action hour four and a half months prior to this day, when the two of them had a rare gap in their schedules and had, in a moment of pent-up desperation, slipped away to the privacy of Phainon's chambers. Mydei was not normally so needy as to seek out sex in the middle of the day, but it had been far too long since they'd laid together.

Phainon had shared his impatience, forgoing all his usual flirtations and pressing him down into the mattress with insistence. Neither of them undressed, just undoing their pants enough to allow access, uncaring of the mess they'd make of themselves. Sweat clung uncomfortably to them both and glittered in beads on bare skin. When Mydei's armored legs squeezed around Phainon's torso, it only seemed to goad him on. He came abruptly-- almost embarrassingly--and then eagerly lowered his head to lap at the mess he'd made until a gauntleted hand was fisted in his hair and Mydei was coming too, just as quickly.

In short, it was brief, rough, and unromantic, more of a stress reliever than anything. If his memory wasn't as good as it is, he probably wouldn't even remember such a brief tangle.

But somehow, it had been the one to defy nature.

Knowing that, it's easy to predict when the child will arrive. There's no need for him to keep track of the days until then with a pocket watch and calendar--the changes in his body are indication enough--but he brought both tools along anyway, just for some sense of normalcy. In these conditions, he reckons it'd be quite easy to lose his mind, and madness is one of the few afflictions his curse cannot mend.

Thankfully, maintaining his sanity isn't a challenge, as there is much to occupy him beyond combat. Survival is the most pressing, and though he has a fair amount of experience, the arduous tasks of hunting and gathering take up a fair portion of his waking hours.

It isn't all difficult, at least. The nearest source of fresh water is a fast flowing creek a short walk from the temple, and after thoroughly cleaning a dusty amphora he scavenged from the ruins, collecting what he needs to drink and bathe is a simple matter.

Getting food requires more effort, as the wildlife is limited and difficult to hunt. At least his skill hasn't degraded in the years since he came to Okhema. All he must do is lodge a long shard of crystalized blood at the space between his quarry's eyes, and so long as his aim is true, it is felled without pain.

Butchering is less familiar to him, and he made a mess of his first kill, a small deer. The smell of its blood, something he believed was unable to bother him, suddenly turned his stomach, and he took far too long quartering the thing, not to mention the shaky cuts made by his unsteady hands.

In the end, he managed to salvage most of the kill. Beyond a portion of a fatty cut that he used while it was fresh to make a stew, he salt-cured the venison in strips, which has insofar lasted him. Berries, nuts, figs, root vegetables, mushrooms, and olives make up the other portion of his diet. He'd make do with less, as it's time-consuming to forage, but he isn't sure if the child within him shares his resilience. It gives him something to do, anyway, and he does appreciate the variety.

Still, his provisions are far from luxurious, and he finds himself daydreaming about the city's delicacies in idle moments. This is temporary, he often reminds himself, so often that it's almost become a mantra.

For now, all he has to do is wait. His plan is rather simple, as he had very little time to come up with it, and he didn't consider anything beyond the logistics, which consist of giving birth in secret and returning with a babe he'll claim he found abandoned in some Tide-stricken village, or something along those lines. He has plenty of time to construct a perfect lie and practice it until he no longer falters.

In moments like these, mired in misery and shivering quietly as the rain thunders down, a part of him wonders if this plan is realistic, or if he has the strength to maintain a lie so heavy for the rest of his life.

Truthfully, he doesn't know. Truthfully, he's more afraid than he's been in a very long time. Truthfully, he's found himself doubting his own resolve, and it has only been a fortnight since his departure.

Was it right of him to run in the first place? The Kremnoans will do fine without him for the next few months--Krateros will step up in his absence-- but there is more to his life than watching over the former detachment. He is a Chrysos Heir. Though the Okhemans once shunned him as a savage, the years have changed that perception, and many now look to him for protection. By clearing out Titankin in Janusopolis, he's certainly protecting, but this by no means guarantees the city's safety.

If something drastic were to happen, he wouldn't even know. The resultant casualties--whose fault would they really be?

Damnit.

Thoughts in this vein are harder to ignore. He tries, desperately, to think of something else, anything else, but the guilt makes it impossible.

At least the rain's stopped for the time-being. He can run from his doubts for a bit longer.

The nearest Titankin is mere paces from the broken door--he launches out to meet it, fist breaching the thin stone of its head and turning it to shrapnel. Its limp body hits the ground with an echoing thud, hairline fractures forming across its broad chest.

His satisfaction is only momentary; when he looks up from the kill, he sees the courtyard full of Titankin now staring him down, alerted by the sound. A half-dozen archers raise their bows in greeting, golden arrows already nocked to taut bowstrings. He lunges forward, the first few shots whizzing right above his head, and the next, aimed lower, narrowly missing his flank out of sheer luck.

Three bounding strides take him to the first archer, sideswept with a gauntlet hard enough to topple it, and a foot stomped through its chest. He falls into a messy side roll to avoid another barrage, landing awkwardly on the corpse's arm in the process--the pain makes him gasp, but he pushes forward, reaching the second archer and throwing it into the third, dispatching both.

The other three are farther away, on the other end of the courtyard, already preparing their next round of arrows. Shit. He sprints five paces before a shot finds its mark in his thigh, causing him to stumble. His legs try to correct course, but he's falling forward, exposed, about to land on his stomach--

He twists in midair, all of his weight driven into his left shoulder instead. He feels the joint shift as he lands, a popping sensation that brings an agonizing surge of pain shooting down his arm. Next is the familiar, nauseating wave of heat, of shock--but he can't let himself feel it. Ignoring every instinct in his body that urges him to remain in place, he forces himself back up with his good arm. All he needs is a breath to ground himself and he's running ahead once more, right fist clenched, winding back, and then thrown forward, obliterating the fourth archer.

The final two have no defenses left with the distance closed. The same number of punches have them joining the rest of their ranks, now all lifeless heaps of stone. He stares down at them, chest heaving with exertion, sweat trickling down his brow.

That was more difficult than it should have been, he thinks.

Then, his legs give out beneath him, and he sinks to the ground.

Only his awareness of his own lightheadedness is what saves him from completely collapsing. He's able to control his descent until he's crouched, knees and right hand pressed against the cool pavement, left arm dangling uselessly by his side.

The issue with it--a dislocation--is obvious from the sensation alone. He'll need to reset it before it can properly heal, he's already aware. In this sense, he's like an ordinary person, accelerated healing aside. Usually, he'd have somebody else around to help, but he'll have to manage alone.

It's a tall order, certainly. Perhaps an impossible one.

He rocks back onto his haunches to assess the injury, and after delicately pushing his himation down his arm, he finds confirmation of a dislocation. The shape of his shoulder is flattened, with his arm pressed strangely into his chest, and he can see the head of the joint jut out below his collarbone. Unmistakeable, really, even to one without medical training.

Beyond a few scrapes, this and the arrow wound are the first injuries he's sustained since his departure. He's surprised it took so long, considering how many Titankin he's been fighting, though he wishes the streak could've lasted a bit longer.

He tries prodding at his shoulder, and swears aloud at the sudden jolt of pain, more intense than he expected. He's aware his pregnancy has weakened his physical capabilities, but it has enhanced them in other, mostly unwelcome, ways. His senses were sharp before, he doesn't need them to be sharper, and he certainly never wanted his pain to hurt worse. Before, he could easily push it from his mind, but now, the twin throbbings in his shoulder and thigh slash his concentration to ribbons, reducing his world to nothing but his labored breathing, his thick swallows, the burn of shock fading away, and of course the rhythmic agony in his tired body. Fixing these injuries is the last thing he wants to do with exhaustion weighing on his mind, but he has no other option.

The arrow will go first, he decides, as he secures his hand against his thigh. Over the course of his life, he estimates he's removed hundreds of arrows. He's so familiar with this sort of injury that he should be able to handle the pain no matter the circumstance.

Or so he thought. When he pulls the arrow from his flesh, the burst of pain is so intense that he has to turn his head to retch violently. Nothing comes up but a bit of acrid saliva he spits onto the pavement; however, the nausea lingers, simmering in the back of his throat. The smell of his ichor in the air does not help. He pulls out his waterskin and douses the area once the puncture has healed over, doing his best to wash away the blood so it can't irritate him anymore.

He knows he's mostly just stalling. His resolve is already weakening. Setting his shoulder will be a hundred times worse than the arrow, he's well aware. If he doesn't do it right this instant, he doesn't think he'll ever manage it, and he has to manage it.

With a shuddering inhale, he closes his hand around his left bicep. Two motions, that's all he needs; he'll pull the top of the bone out from where it's lodged and do his best to push it back up into place. His body isn't too picky, it just has to be close enough to the socket for healing to commence.

Just close enough.

After another steadying breath, he yanks hard.

Immediately, a terrible lance of pain cleaves through his body, so terrible it batters against his mind, rips at the edges of his consciousness and his sanity itself, consuming each piece of him in sequence as he falls apart. It's almost too raw to process, a sensation--if such a word can even describe how much it is--that reaches to extremities and tangles itself up like a trapped animal.

And it's not yet done. With the last dredges of strength left in his body, he pushes his arm up, wordlessly praying to whatever Titan might be listening for it to take, for whatever force that allows his flesh to mend itself to work its magic and finish the job. Each second that passes is a small eternity, and he almost loses his willpower, almost, but then he feels it, that deep twist and shift of tissue inside of him, pulling the head of the joint back into place.

But there is still no relief. His vision is static. His blood roars in his ears. He feels each desperate thud of his heart racing away in his frozen ribcage. Forcing himself to breathe is near impossible--he begins to cough, to gag, choking on the air itself. The muscles are weaving themselves back around the socket, and though it's welcome, it all hurts, he can't think, he can do nothing but writhe helplessly in the face of this merciless pain.

He isn't sure if he truly faints--the darkness is impossible to parse in the throes of agony. All he knows is that, eventually, the pain is nothing but a dull ache, and he's lying flat on his back, staring up at the darkened sky.

Slowly, he sits up. An experimental shift of his shoulder reveals it to be a bit stiff, but it seems to be properly healed. A few hours of rest should bring it back to normal.

That, at least, is a relief. Everything else about his current situation is displeasing. He's entirely sapped of strength, to the extent that he doesn't think he has the ability to make it all the way back to his safe room. Though the mere idea makes him grimace, it seems he'll need to recover his strength in one of the nearby houses. They're all rotting away and are certainly dirty, not to mention the danger of sleeping in an area he knows hasn't been cleared of Titankin.

"Whatever, you can handle it," he mutters to himself, mostly for the comfort of hearing his own voice. He's been doing that a lot lately. Perhaps it's not good for his psyche, but the prospect of complete silence feels more daunting.

He continues to mumble things as he surveys a few of the houses, pointing out the flaws as he pokes around. Most of them are entirely unsuitable, but eventually, he finds a promising one; the roof doesn't seem to be leaking, and on the first floor, there's an intact kline with a few worn pillows laying atop it. They're rather dusty, but simply shaking them out does the trick.

It's far from luxury, but after a final look around, he deems the place acceptable. He can stand to sleep here.

Before he settles down, he musters up the willpower to drag a large wardrobe in front of the door, just in case a wandering Titankin detects his presence. The blockade won't do much to stop it, but it'll make enough noise in the process of breaking through that he'll have time to get his bearings.

He briefly considers securing the door with additional furniture, but exhaustion drags at his body, and he can do nothing but lay down upon the kline, slipping into a dreamless sleep the moment his eyes slide shut.

"Hey, look! There's Titankin corpses over here."

Mydei is roused some indeterminate amount of time later by the sound of faint conversation. His sleep-addled mind is quick to dismiss it as the chatter of passing travelers, and he closes his bleary eyes, intent on resting for a bit longer.

"Whoever dispatched them is quite strong. An ordinary person isn't capable of destroying their bodies in such a way... A trained warrior, then?"

"Perhaps, though any old warrior also couldn't do this, I'd reckon... But there's no red crystals around, so I don't think it was him."

"You were hoping this was Lord Mydei's doing?"

"Yeah, I was. I know I'm... ugh, I'm being stupid about all of this. I'm sorry, Castorice."

Suddenly, Mydei is fully awake. He wants to deny what he just heard, but he can't ignore the familiarity of these two voices, not with the confirmation of a name.

Phainon and Castorice are here. They're here, and they're coming closer.

"You don't need to apologize. I miss him as well, we all do," Castorice says softly. Mydei does his best to reign in his mounting panic. He needs to stay calm, stay still.

"But I feel like I'm not focusing on this mission. We're not here for Mydei! We're here to help people," Phainon exclaims, and dear gods, does hearing that voice make him feel weak.

"Technically, locating Mydei is the goal of every mission Aglaea's been sending out, no matter what the official reason may be."

A pause. Mydei strains his ears, listening to their distant footfalls and hoping beyond belief that they don't come any closer while knowing that they likely will. Two of the Titankin he felled were positioned right outside this house.

"You're right. I feel so selfish, but it's not very selfish to want to find him."

"Even if it was selfish, it would be okay."

Another pause.

"... Thank you."

Phainon sounds so broken, and something in Mydei breaks too. All his uncertainties claw at his mind, asking him if he thinks this is really okay, if he should just push his way out of the door and show himself, if he should finally put an end to this deception-- --but he stamps it all down as quickly as it arose by simply recalling his rejection. He can't risk anything, not with Phainon.

The fear of losing him is one so terrible that it often robs Mydei of sleep, instead lying supine and tensed in his nest of blankets, anxiety gnawing away at his insides. After a life full of loss, he never thought he'd take a person for granted again, and yet, Phainon's presence became a constant so steady that he found it impossible to imagine himself without his other half.

If there is a selfish one between the two of them, it is Mydei. All of this is for his own benefit, just so he can birth this child, bring them before Phainon while lying about their origins, and raise them on his own without his lover feeling any sense of obligation to help.

In his mind, the child will always be theirs, but Phainon doesn't need to know, not if fatherhood will hurt him.

Mydei has to keep hiding.

The footfalls get louder. He grits his teeth together and bites back a string of curses. Of course they're coming to investigate the corpses, godsdamnit.

He doesn't dare move. His breathing is slow and painfully shallow, just enough to keep himself conscious. Even blinking feels like a mistake.

He's done everything to avoid this, though he should've known from the beginning that his efforts would be futile. If he could just lay low, hide out deep within Janusopolis where no souls dare venture, clean up the Titankin he leaves behind, and not utilize his more conspicuous abilities, he believed he could stop the other Chrysos Heirs from investigating--but why wouldn't they? If another of their rank is missing, they'll search for them everywhere, even in the most unlikely of places.

"The force used for these kills... Maybe it wasn't done by a human at all. Aren't there beasts that'll target Titankin when provoked?" Phainon asks, startling Mydei. They're mere meters away from him now, separated only by the worn stone wall. He can hear them shifting around as they presumably investigate the corpses.

"Griffins, manticores, and basilisks will, if the accounts I read are accurate. I've not seen them do it myself, but all of them are certainly capable of such violence."

So long as they don't lapse into complete silence, there should be no chance of them hearing him; as for smelling him, he thinks they would've mentioned it by now if they could. The stale air hides most scents, he's come to learn, and any lingering traces are quickly gusted off by the sporadic, strong winds.

"Yeah... It just seems awfully convenient that some wandering beast swooped in and killed Titankin in the exact area we were meant to clear. The Fates work in mysterious ways, I suppose."

The footsteps restart, slowly proceeding whence they came. Relief courses through him.

And then, something inside of him moves.

It is a miracle he doesn't make much of a sound. One hand clasps over his mouth while the other flies down to grasp at the swell of his abdomen, at the place where he feels it, that utterly foreign sensation immediately recognizable as his child's tiny movements.

Something that should fill him with joy instead fills him with terror. He knows he gasped, just slightly, and the pair must've heard it, as their footsteps have halted. It's far too quiet in the aftermath; his own heartbeat thunders so loudly in his chest that he fears it must be audible.

"... Did you hear something?"

Castorice's question is the nail in the coffin. Dread rises like a tide within him and he can do nothing but wait for the sound of their re-approaching, for they'll surely investigate the sound.

"I didn't, but you've got better ears than me. Do you think there's an enemy nearby?"

"I don't know..."

Her words linger heavily in the air, and the silence stretches on, each passing second a small eternity. Mydei isn't certain if he'll survive it. He's never been a pious man, but he prays to each Titan in quick succession, knowing that only a miracle will save him now.

Castorice has spent a millenia honing her senses; now that she has reason to suspect a living being may be nearby, it's certain that she'll detect the quiet hum of his biological machinery, of pumping blood and contracting muscles, the barest traces that are impossible to suppress.

It's over, he thinks, already resigning himself to whatever fate is about to befall him. Most of what he feels is regret, and he's used to its sting by now. It's his own fault for running with such a hasty plan. If he spent more than a quint hashing it out instead of caving to his desperation to flee Okhema, he would've anticipated this, and then he wouldn't have to lose--

"Never mind. It was just the wind."

The relief from her words is so unexpected that it doesn't quite register, and Mydei waits for the miracle to collapse, for what could it be but some twisted mirage--but it holds steady.

"My apologies for startling you, Lord Phainon," Castorice continues, "I've just felt a bit strange since we got to Janusopolis."

"It's alright, I've felt strange as well... Good to know I'm not the only one. It just seems too quiet. Something must be up here, what with the lack of Titankin and the lack of their corpses, I mean..."

Finally, they egress out of earshot. Mydei doesn't dare move, not yet, not until his muscles burn from the discomfort of staying in place for so long and he lets himself slowly adjust to a sitting position, feet planted solidly on the ground.

Fuck.

Even now, he doesn't feel relieved. That was far, far too close. Sheer luck saved him, and he's never liked leaving things up to chance.

He needs to leave this courtyard; loitering any longer is just begging for trouble, as Phainon and Castorice could easily double back. He can only hope that they won't travel so deep into Janusopolis that they'll stumble across his safe room, though that seems rather unlikely.

With some trepidation, he pushes the wardrobe away from the door and eases it open. Of course, the child chooses this moment to move again, startling him enough to let go of the handle. He's unsure if he'll ever adjust to the sensation. It feels almost like a muscle twitching, but deeper in his body, moreso as if one of his organs has acquired a mind of its own.

It's strange, yes, and it makes him smile. His child is thriving within him, growing stronger by the day. What a gift it is to have been born an omega, so he can carry this blossoming life within his own womb. They may not have picked the best moment to make their presence known, but that's no fault of their own.

He feels no other movements as he quietly makes his way back to the safe room, nor while he prepares himself a quick meal, not in the mood for laboring over the fire for a quint. Checking his pocket watch informs him that this is a late dinner, and he'd typically turn in afterwards, but having just napped, he doesn't yet feel sleepy, just mentally exhausted.

So, he makes the climb up to the slanted roof of the temple to stargaze. There's a sizable hole at one end, and the exposed joists are large enough for him to sit upon, offering an excellent vantage point.

The light pollution from the Dawn Device is bad enough to block out most of the stars, but off in the distance, a smattering can still be seen through the gaps in the clouds. He's spent many of his idle moments up here, letting his mind wander, sometimes thinking of consequential matters and sometimes of nothing much at all. He oft did the same on the rooftops of Okhema; it has always helped him to gather himself.

Today, he has much to consider, yet his traitorous thoughts drift elsewhere, to a thing he shouldn't: his fear.

"You will naturally have fears in your life, but you should never let them fester in your mind--grab them by the neck and toss them away the moment they appear. Ignore them entirely. Let them know they shall never have any power over you. One day, the part of you which conjures them up will shrivel up from disuse, and your body will no longer know fear," Krateros had advised him many years ago, soon after he'd clambered out of the Sea of Souls. The lesson has always stuck with him, as it is the one he has always failed to follow.

He has tried, of course. Still tries every day. How lovely would it be if that frightened part of him had withered away, but he doesn't think it will. For a man whose first memories are not the terror of dying endlessly to the violent sea, perhaps it could, but for Mydei, he has known fear too intimately to ever lose it.

And there is a new fear, a terrible one. It has quickly taken root as his pregnancy has become more obvious, and the concept of fatherhood solidifies in his mind. He's desperate to reject it, to assure himself that such a thing is entirely impossible, but it only seems to entrench itself deeper, like some insidious toxin.

How could he ever fear that he may become like his father, knowing the full extent of his treachery? No twisted prophecy with a demand to slaughter his own child weighs on his mind, no corruption has infested his heart, and yet, a voice tells him that it could, that he could lose himself just as Eurypon did, that he very well could shun the life he carries.

His child deserves better than him, a prince born from a legacy of death.

Or perhaps he will make a fine father, and he's overthinking the entire matter. Though the latter is more likely, no amount of reason can satisfy him.

If Phainon were here, he might just manage.

But he isn't. Mydei watches the stars alone, carrying a child unwanted by its other father.

Chapter End Notes
