chapters.html:
Phainon's head hurts.

As he eases into wakefulness, he wishes he could return right back to sleep, if only to hide from the relentless throbbing in his temples. It's not just his head; his mouth is impossible dry, his stomach pangs with hunger, and every muscle in his body aches from overexertion.

Dear Titans, he feels awful. A sad whimper is torn from his lips before he can stifle it, and he can only hope that there's nobody around to hear it.

He's not even sure where he is right now--his mind is addled by both sleep and discomfort, too muddled to think past the pain. Wherever he decided to rest is far from ideal, though he doesn't wish to open his eyes and find out. Kephale's light shines harshly against his closed eyelids, exacerbating his headache as is. He manages to flop a limp hand across his face to block it out.

At some point, he'll have to get up, he's well aware. He doesn't really want to think that far ahead yet, not until he's remembered how to be a person.

Unfortunately for him, the world isn't going to wait for him to be ready. Something--or someone--has removed the hand over his face and begun poking his cheek.

"Snowy, are you awake now? Open your eyes!"

He thinks Lady Tribbie might be speaking to him, but he's not quite sure. Her voice sounds tinny and dreamlike in a way that makes it hard to understand.

"... What did you say?" he mumbles, words slurring together into mush despite his attempts to annunciate them. His tongue feels less like a muscle and more like a packed wad of clay. He swallows hard, trying to get some saliva back into his mouth, and determines that he's quite dehydrated.

"Uh, well... We didn't understand what he just said, but he seems to be waking up!"

"That's a relief. Thank you for your assistance, Lady Tribbie."

Is Castorice here too? It seems he might have an audience wherever it is that he's ended up. He finally manages to crack open his eyes, and finds that indeed, both Lady Tribbie and Castorice are staring at him, with the former hovering right over his face, and the latter barely visible in his periphery.

It seems he's lying on a stone bench in a secluded courtyard, which is far from the most comfortable place to take a nap. That explains why the back of his skull aches worse than the rest of his head, at least.

With the confirmation, he decides to shut his eyes again. Kephale's light is way too bright, just as he thought it might be, and his vignetted vision doesn't take well to it.

"No, don't go back to sleep!" Tribbie cries.

"I'm awake, just resting my eyes," he assures her, this time managing to speak more clearly. "I've got a headache."

Castorice hums in acknowledgement. "I see. It's good to see you're finally conscious. Thank you for your help, Lady Tribbie. You can return to your errand now."

"He still seems... Well, if you're certain. Call us back if Snowy needs a few more pokes. Bye bye, Cas!"

Phainon listens to Tribbie flutter away, which he laments. He can feel the weight of Castorice's gaze on him now that it's just the two of them.

"Lord Phainon."

"I know. I know I need to take better care of myself."

He immediately regrets how snappish his tone is. There's no reason to be confrontational.

"... I'm sorry. I'm not trying to upset you, I'm simply worried."

"Ugh, no--I'm sorry, I'm not mad at you," he groans, opening his eyes to find Castorice wearing a tight frown. "I really do appreciate the concern, it's nice to know you care so much about me!"

Thankfully, her frown eases up a bit, and her expression turns contemplative. "Alright. Shall we get some lunch, then?"

The sudden change in topic gives him pause; although he's automatically poised to reject the offer, his hunger is gnawing relentlessly at his midsection, and it's difficult to ignore.

When was the last time he ate, anyway? He had dinner the previous evening, but today, he was so preoccupied by tracking leads in the Kremnoan district that he only had the time to eat a pomegranate somebody gifted him. That may be part of the reason why he passed out on this random bench, though the compounding lack of sleep definitely hasn't helped.

His life is falling apart, dear gods. He needs to get his act together before his body gives out on him entirely.

So, they end up at the nearest diner--a place that Phainon's not been to before--seated at a spacious table. It's empty enough that Castorice doesn't have to worry about her proximity to others, and they're also afforded a fair amount of privacy once the waiter leaves with their orders.

The silence between them settles, rather uncomfortably, as they wait for their food. Phainon drains his water cup to occupy himself, and then, once his thirst is slaked, he looks awkwardly around the restaurant, hands twisting together in his lap. He wants to say something, anything to dispel the tension, but nothing comes to mind. There's nothing left for him to say that Castorice doesn't know. She's watched him work himself to the bone for the past few weeks, and he's ignored her and everyone else trying to reign him back.

For whatever reason, being here, in this little diner, with Castorice staring him down, has brought him a fair amount of clarity. He's not sure if he's happy to have it. Now, he's just embarrassed.

"Have you found any leads recently?" Castorice asks, before he can bow before her and profusely apologize for his recent behavior.

"Still nothing. None of the Kremnoans know anything. They all want to help, of course, but they can't offer more than conjecture on where Mydei's gone or why he left in the first place."

"Then perhaps you should pause the search for a while. Information can passively gather while you rest."

It's the last thing he wants to do, and based on her wariness to suggest it, he presumes that Castorice can sense his reluctance. The concept of relaxing while Mydei's out there somewhere, certainly alone and possibly suffering, is unbearable. The fact that the search has drawn on as long as it already has is unbearable enough. He doesn't want to prolong it.

But what use is he while he's like this? He's in no shape to fight; he's barely well enough to manage a walk around the city. Only an idiot would press on in this condition.

"You're right. I'll pause the search."

Castorice's eyes widen. "Oh, I... I didn't expect you to agree. I'm sorry if I was too insistent, you shouldn't feel pressured to do anything."

"You were far from insistent. You just spoke the truth, and I'm finally tired enough to listen. Frankly, I should've listened weeks ago. I should be the one apologizing for... for everything, really. I know I've been short with all of you, and impossible to work with, and absent more often than not, and... I mean, just awful all around."

"Please don't be so hard on yourself, we all understand why you're upset."

"Me being upset doesn't excuse my behavior."

"But this goes beyond just being upset!" she says, her voice as emphatic as he's ever heard it. "I know I've understated how you must feel--Lord Mydei is very special to you. He's not your mate, but you're as close as a bonded pair, and the pain of losing someone you treasure so dearly isn't ignorable."

"... I know. It's just... It feels like this is all my fault, somehow. How can I mourn something that I caused?"

Castorice's brow scrunches. "No matter the circumstance, it doesn't preclude you from mourning his absence, but what do you mean?"

"Before he disappeared, he was avoiding me, and really only me. Maybe there's no connection and I'm blaming myself for nothing... I just can't shake the thought."

"I suppose it's a possibility, though you said yourself that he was acting strangely the moment he returned from the expedition, so I can't imagine what you could've done," she replies. At this point, the repeated attempt at comfort fails, though it's not any fault of her own.

For weeks, he's felt as if he's teetering on the brink of realization, felt that he's surrounded by evidence and if he pushes just a bit more, he'll stumble his way right into the answer. What happened, and why--shouldn't he know by now? After all he's seen Mydei do since his return, he should've learned enough to piece it together, but he just can't. The clues don't fit together so neatly.

There must be something he's missing, some possibility so obvious yet so impossible that he's not yet considered it, not even allowed it to cross his mind. His own ignorance goads him onward just as it torments him, and he can't take it.

Phainon buries his head in his hands and makes a frustrated noise into his palms. "This is too complicated, I can't handle it right now. I feel sick."

"Ah, I'm sorry. Is there a specific reason for your malaise beyond a lack of rest that I didn't consider? Perhaps your, uh, cycle?"

"No, it's not pre-rut, I've just exhausted myself. I'd know if it was my cycle, I mean, I..."

Wait.

When was he last due for a rut?

"Then perhaps we... Lord Phainon, are you feeling alright?"

"I, uh, realized... Give me one second, Castorice," he mumbles, as he yanks his teleslate from his pocket and flips to the calendar. He's never been the best at tracking his cycles, but he tries to note down each time his pre-rut starts, just in case something were to happen--and right now is that something.

He hopes he's just mistaken, that his last rut wasn't more than a few months ago and he's completely misremembering things. After all, he's been so busy lately, it's only natural that his memories would get scrambled up--

"I was due for my last rut almost a month ago, and it never happened."

"Oh. Oh my... That isn't good."

They stare at each other for a moment that seems to stretch into eternity. Phainon's mind, made sluggish by overwork, can't quite process the realization. Something terrible might be happening to him, and he doesn't know what to do other than stew in his unease.

His rut has never been late. It's as reliable as clockwork, coming at the same time every three months like an unwelcome but familiar acquaintance. No matter how grief-stricken, stressed, or upset he's been, it has never once wavered.

"... I should probably go see Lady Hyacine," he manages, voice coming out shakier than he'd like.

"You should eat your food first, though. I don't believe skipping a meal will make it better."

He's not sure how much of an appetite he has left, but Castorice is right. When the waiter finally arrives with their meals, he manages to stomach most of it with sheer hunger motivating him despite the tightness in his throat. Only a few bites remain when he finally gives up.

"I'll pay for us both, you can go to Lady Hyacine," Castorice says as he sets down his fork. "Please don't worry about paying me back right now." For once, he doesn't insist, and after a rushed farewell, leaves Castorice behind at the diner.

By some stroke of luck, it appears that Hyacine's infirmary in the city is open. Phainon breathes a sigh of relief when the doorknob yields under his hand. He's not sure why she's in Okhema, but he won't look a gift dromas in the mouth. He doesn't trust another doctor with such a personal issue, and not having to travel all the way to the Grove is a blessing.

However, when he steps into the clinic, he finds the waiting room and the space behind the front desk vacant. His heart immediately sinks. It doesn't bode well, but since the door was unlocked, he can only assume Hyacine's here. With some apprehension, he rings the service bell; a second later, Little Ica pops up from somewhere behind the desk with a disgruntled trill, presumably awakened from its nap.

"Ah, Ica! It's good to see you, my friend. Is Hyacine available to see me today? I've got an urgent problem."

Ica makes a noise that, at the very least, sounds affirmative, and flies off into the clinic. Phainon's not sure what to do in its absence. He takes a seat in the nearest chair, assuming that it may take a while for it to reappear.

That assumption ends up being untrue, as only a few minutes later, Hyacine emerges from the back with Ica fluttering behind her, looking a bit frazzled. "Are you alright, Lord Phainon? Ica seems worried for you."

"Lady Hyacine, it's... Well, I'm not sure how big of an issue it might be. If you're busy right now, I can wait," he assures her, to no avail. He must look unwell enough for his words to fall flat.

"I was packing up to return to the Grove, but I only just started, I can still see you today. Come to the examination room, please tell me what the matter is."

He waits until the door of the examination room clicks shut before he finally opens his mouth to speak. "It's about my rut. It was due to start almost a month ago, but I still haven't had my pre-rut."

Her reaction to those words is not what he expected, mostly because she has a reaction. Her stoic, unshakeable expression cracks, and though she reigns in her surprise only a moment later, he's still taken off-guard by the widening of her eyes.

"Lord Phainon, you're aware that..."

A pause. Again, Hyacine's expression morphs, her mouth parting in something that seems like realization.

"Oh... I see. Is it alright if I exam you quickly? I'd like to check the scent glands on the sides of your neck, please."

He's confused by her actions, but he turns around and cranes his neck to allow her access. Her hands are ice-cold against the sensitive skin; he fails to suppress a shudder.

"I know it's uncomfortable, but please keep your neck still... Thank you. You've never had a mating mark, or been mated, right?"

"No, Mydei and I are just partners. I was planning to mate with him, but... I can't exactly do that right now."

"I'm very sorry about that, by the way. I do hope Lord Mydei returns soon," she says quietly, as she continues to prod at his scent glands. "It's possible that he may have something to do with your absent rut."

"How so?"

"Well, even though you're not mated, sometimes you will respond to your partner's own body as if you were. Mydei emits pheromones that are detected by your nose and vomeronasal organ, and this sends signals to your body to respond in certain ways. A mating bite would change the profile of the pheromones released by his scent glands and therefore change your body's response, but even without the bite, an alpha's body still has sensitivity to an omega's existing pheromones. With enough time spent around the same omega, the body will learn and adjust to their unique chemical profile, both mentally and physically.

"All of that is to say that you are pseudomated. That is my belief, anyway. If you'd allow me to swab your scent glands, I can run a test to confirm."

"Please do."

It seems a bit complicated to someone like him, who knows so woefully little about dynamics, but plausible enough. He puzzles over it while Hyacine runs a cotton swab over his neck and sticks it into a small vial of liquid. He and Mydei have spent a lot of time together in the last few years, that is true, and they certainly act like a mated couple with how they scent and nest.

Phainon isn't sure why they never took the leap and bonded with each other. He has always hesitated when the opportunity presented itself. Mydei never seized the chance either; honestly, Phainon was waiting for him to do it. Perhaps there's some Kremnoan cultural significance to it.

It's not like it matters much anymore, if Hyacine's right. Their bodies decided they'd be mates, regardless of how their minds acted. And if they're mates, then what does that mean for Phainon?

"If we are psuedomated, why would that delay my rut?" he asks, while watching Hyacine swirl the vial lightly in one hand.

"There are a few different reasons. I can run some bloodwork to see if it's due to a hormonal disorder, but I strongly suspect that isn't the case, since your scent doesn't have any atypical qualities. I believe it's stress related, as there is a level of physiological stress one endures when their mate is absent for a prolonged period. Therefore, I don't have any concerns for your health."

"Alright, I trust you," he replies, nodding as if he fully accepts the explanation.

But he doesn't.

Hyacine's lying to him about something. The way she flinched, ever so slightly, when he asked his question was indication enough. The way she wouldn't meet his gaze while talking was the nail in the coffin.

He's so taken off guard by it all that he doesn't bother to press, even though he definitely should. In a daze, he listens to her give him a clean bill of health and send him out of the clinic with a cheery farewell, too lost in thought to properly focus.

That entire conversation was bizarre. Somehow, all Hyacine did was confuse him further. Lying aside, she offered him none of the answers he sought--really, she just gave him a new question to add to his ever-growing pile.

"Lord Phainon, you're aware that..."

Is he aware of what?

Gods, this is driving him insane. He needs to go to the baths and relax for a while before his skull cracks open from the stress.

At this time of day, the main floor of the Mamoreal Palace is far too busy for his liking, and he makes a beeline to the Heroes' baths. Hopefully, the divine waters will help with his pounding headache. He's pleased to find it empty, and after informing the nearest attendant that he'd like to be left alone today, he casts off his clothes and reclines in the deepest section of the pool.

His headache eases quickly, much to his relief, but unfortunately, his emotions must be too volatile for the water to soothe. Perhaps he needs to wait longer than half of a quint for that effect. Aglaea had some sort of warning about not staying too long in the baths, but she's not here, so he can probably get away with--

"Lord Phainon, you seem awfully troubled."

Or perhaps not. The water's tranquil surface is disturbed as Aglaea lowers herself in a respectful distance away, just close enough to carry out a conversion. He should've known she'd arrive around this time; her schedule is quite busy, but it's also predictable.

"More troubled than I've been the last few weeks?"

She hums. "Troubled in a different matter. You're trying to figure something out, yes?"

"Yeah," he confesses, knowing there's no reason to keep it from her. "Perhaps you can lend me your ear? I think you might be able to give me some advice."

"Go ahead, I'll see if I can."

"It's just that... My rut is extremely late, and it's never been late before. I mean, I'm stressed out right now, and that could be the reason, but still, it doesn't feel right to write it off like that. Something else is going on, I'm sure. So, I went to Lady Hyacine, since I thought she'd probably know. And, well... I really think she knows why, but she won't tell me. She just said it was due to stress... A lie of omission, I suppose."

"You're certain she lied?"

"Quite so. You've taught me well, Lady Aglaea, I know how to read a person's tells."

"Curious. Lady Hyacine would not typically lie to a patient, and not to a friend, either. For her to do so must mean something very important is on the line, perhaps involving another patient's confidentiality."

Aglaea says nothing else for a while, perhaps sensing that Phainon is deep in thought, and perhaps knowing that she may not need to say anything else. All she really needed to do was give him a nudge to jump-start his thinking.

Something very important, huh.

It involves Mydei's confidentiality; of course, it always comes back to him in the end. Phainon watches the placid ripples on the surface of the water, mind working to lay out all the pieces of the puzzle as neatly as he can manage, starting at the beginning.

Mydei returned after his expedition and began acting strangely. That's the impetus for everything. Something must've happened during it, or so Phainon assumed, but he might be thinking about it the wrong way. The other clues don't necessarily suggest that. He shouldn't take it as an absolute.

What does he know without any conjecture? That is where he should start. It has been quite a few years since his time at the Grove, but he remembers a fair portion of what he learned, and he'd never forget something that Anaxa was relentless in correcting.

Unfortunately, there aren't many facts to establish. Mydei suddenly began wearing different clothes. He left a meeting due to what seemed to be some sort of illness, despite the fact that, by his own admission, he's immune to disease. He acted cagey around Phainon for a few days before he ended up avoiding him completely. He spoke with Hyacine and then promptly disappeared from the city.

The wardrobe change is the strangest fact; it's certainly important, but it's still hard to fathom. Why would Mydei hide his body when he was perfectly content to flaunt it in the past? Perhaps there was some change there that displeased him, or a change that he believed might displease others. His scent, too, had changed, but not in an emotional way. There was no harsh tang of anger, no subtle stink of depression. What can be conveyed through one's scent beyond emotion? Phainon's unsure, but-- Could it relate to that mysterious illness of his? What condition might cause illness--without being an actual illness--while also changing one's body and scent in a distinct way? What condition could affect one's mate as well?

And what condition would get more noticeable over time, unknown to everyone at first but slowly appearing, growing over the course of months? What condition might incubate for long enough as to not be at all evident upon departing for a long expedition, instead revealed later in its duration?

Is Mydei--

Oh Titans.

Oh, dear Titans above.

Phainon thought it would be more satisfying to realize the truth, but no, it is a terrible thing, slowly blanketing him, crushing him underneath its suffocating weight.

He thinks there's only one question left to ask, and he barely has the strength to ask it. His stomach is beginning to ache. His chest burns with the air of his last inhale. His heart hammers nauseatingly. His eyes lock onto Aglaea's unseeing gaze, flailing for any sort of comfort that he's already aware he won't find.

"... What's the main reason that an alpha would miss their rut?" he asks, almost inaudible. There's a tremor to his voice. Aglaea hears it all, knows his fear in an instant. Her tone is as even as always when she replies.

"For an unmated alpha, there's a plethora of reasons... but if they are mated, and they don't have any health problems, it would be due to their mate becoming pregnant."

"... Aglaea."

"Yes, Phainon?"

"Aglaea," he says again, more insistent, more desperate, as he tries to force the words out. "Mydei's pregnant. And he--he thinks... He thinks I don't want it. That's why he left. I told him--oh gods, Aglaea, I told him I didn't want kids with him but it wasn't because I didn't want that, it's because I was scared of--of what might happen and I--"

"Phainon, breathe," she commands, firmly enough to slow the cascading tide of his thoughts, but just barely. He tries, damnit, he tries so hard to calm himself. Panicking won't fix it. Panicking feels like the only thing he can do.

More than a year ago, Mydei suggested that they have children, and Phainon refused point-blank. He wanted a family so badly that it frightened him. To love somebody that wasn't Mydei--the one thing that death could not take from him--was dangerous.

More than a year later, Phainon no longer feels that same fear, and yet, he failed where it mattered the most. He never bothered to explain to Mydei exactly how he felt back then, never assured him that he'd finally beaten down that part of him that refused comfort out of the belief that he'd lose it all in the end, never promised him that he'd remain steadfast by his side.

The consequence of that? Mydei fled. He must've been so worried about how Phainon would react to the news, having seen how he managed the subject in the past, that leaving seemed to be a safer option.

How did Phainon fuck this up so badly? Mydei's pregnancy should've been a celebration, not this.

"I have to go find him now. He's out in the Evernight alone and he's pregnant and it's my fault!" he cries, already clambering from the bath with frantic movements and splashing divine water all across the tile.

"You're in no shape to leave the city," Aglaea insists, "we'll send a search party in your stead, you need to rest."

He ignores her in favor of toweling himself off.

"Phainon, stop," she insists, more forcefully this time, with a dangerous edge to her tone. He does stop, and he whips his head around to glare at her, because there's something in her words--a too-composed calmness--that makes anger spark up within him.

"... Did you know?"

Her expression does not change. She doesn't shift an inch. Phainon may have learned to read others well, but she remains impossibly out of reach. Still, despite the impeccable facade, he can discern enough for the anger to burn brighter.

"You knew, didn't you--and you didn't... You didn't tell anyone!"

"I had my suspicions, but that is not enough evidence to work on."

"But you should've--"

"Should've done more than I did already? Allowing you to search for him was all that was in my capabilities, no matter the information available. Would you have done anything differently if you had known he was with child? I suspect you'd have only worked yourself harder."

"And it would've been my right to do so!" he shouts. After facing down his exhaustion just an hour prior, he knows he should be much more rational about this, but the sudden surge of protectiveness has him throwing away all logic.

"I will not allow you to work yourself into an early grave, no matter how much you insist upon it."

"I know my limits, I won't."

It's a ridiculous thing for him to say when it's so obvious that he doesn't. His own petulance sobers him up a bit; he shouldn't act like this in front of Aglaea, somehow who knows so much about him and how his mind ticks.

Her quiet sigh is a good indication that he's exasperated her. "Phainon, I'm not trying to act as your enemy right now. I'm trying to prevent you from making a mistake. Mydeimos will not be helped by poor planning, none of us will."

"I... I know," he acquiesces, "I understand why you didn't tell me. But you can't stop me from searching right now. This is my responsibility. Send out a search party if you want, but I'm going."

She considers his words for a long moment. If she really wanted to stop him from leaving, she and her golden threads could certainly stop him. He probably should've been less confrontational with her, but she can sense the depth of his conviction regardless of what he says.

"Please, just be careful," she finally says. "Don't search anywhere that's excessively dangerous, not alone."

"Don't worry, I'm not going to take risks. I'm going to find him. We're both coming home safe."

He can only hope that his determination will be enough.

chapters.html:
When Mydei wakes, he's nauseous.

Of course, the feeling is now all too familiar. It would almost be strange to wake without its sickly chill lingering in his gut and clinging to the back of his throat, though that isn't to suggest it's welcome.

He truly thought it would've vanished by now, so far into the second trimester. Taking a pill of Hyacine's medication every other night still eases it enough to prevent him from vomiting and allows him to forget his nausea for most of the day, but the supply in the bottle is dwindling. At this rate, it seems his morning sickness is bound to outlast the medicine.

His future seems unpleasant, to say the least. Nightmarish may be more apt of a descriptor. Certainly, imagining it does not make him feel any better. Even with the pills, his mornings are far from pleasant.

As is routine, Mydei lays on his back for the first few minutes of wakefulness, staring up at the temple's ruined ceiling and doing his best to breathe evenly through his nose. The child is squirming around inside of him, which isn't helping; since they first moved two weeks ago, they've begun a constant assault on his insides.

In hindsight, he should've anticipated this. Any child with two accomplished warriors for parents will be a feisty one. He supposes he prefers the movement to a lack of it, even if it sometimes bothers him.

Eventually, they still, and the nausea eases enough for him to clamber to his feet and properly start his day. He doesn't have much of a schedule to adhere to out here, but even so, he doesn't want to stall. Idle hands are his worst enemy.

A quick soak in the creek by his safe house is first on the docket, helping to shake off the last dredges of groginess and also dispel some of the nausea. It helps a fair amount, though his stomach still feels a bit touchy as he prepares a small, simple breakfast. Not eating will be worse in the long run, he reminds himself, as he chokes it down. He'll need abundant energy for what he has planned.

Clearing the Titankin from one of the largest temples in Janusopolis is the next great undertaking, and he's planned for it carefully. Now that he's reached the fifth month of pregnancy, he's been more fatigued and become less agile; the longer he waits to do this, the more weighed down he'll be.

Thankfully, after thoroughly scoping out the temple, he thinks he has a plan that won't require too much work or risk on his part. All it will take is some quick effort.

With a bag of supplies slung over his shoulder and a round of stretching behind him that does little to help the persistent twinge in his lower back, he begins the trek through the city. The decrepit streets once bustled with Titankin activity, but they're peaceful now; over the past month, the results of constant hunting have gone from negligible to unmistakable. Inevitably, monsters will move back in, but until then, passing refugees should be able to find some safety.

If even a single life is saved from his efforts, it will have been worth it. And for now, he enjoys the moment of calm before the inevitable storm.

Before he's even stepped through the broken-open doors of the temple, he's faced with a sizable group of Titankin loitering on the steps outside. Unfortunately--or fortunately--these ones will have to be dealt with by hand. He flexes his fingers, then allows them to curl into tight fists as his body falls into the dance of combat.

The single archer standing by the outskirks is his first target, grabbed by the arm and tossed into the main hoard, felling a few warriors and confusing the others. They're still hesitating, examining the archer's corpse, when Mydei descends upon them, crushing them with well-aimed punches.

It's a quick, brutal fight. Only one warrior even managed to swing at him, and they missed by a mile. Triumphant, he marches over their ruined, ichor-soaked bodies to where the temple awaits.

For once, he needs to employ some amount of stealth, lest he want to turn this simple mission into an arduous bloodbath. It will be a bloodbath regardless, but he doesn't plan on being an active participant.

It begins at the temple's center, where a massive brazier, still brimming with coals, lays cold and dead. Mydei passes through a network of side hallways to reach it, avoiding the Titankin he sees and silently dispatching the ones in his way. It's remarkably easy to behead them, he's found, so long as one pulls at the right angle and twists with enough force.

This temple has remained mostly intact, including its maze-like interior; despite coming through here multiple times, he still gets lost, stumbling across prayer rooms, vaults, and libraries he's never before found. It's more of a struggle than he'd like to admit, but he stumbles upon his destination eventually.

The central room is cavernous, and in the darkness, it seems to be endless, shadows stretching infinitely outward. From that yawning void, the sounds of shifting Titankin echo unnervingly, allowing one's mind to run wild in imagining just how many hundreds might lie in wait.

Mydei's afforded very little room for error in this endeavor.

His first, and only, goal: light the brazier. With the flint packed in his bag, it's theoretically an easy job, but there's no way to walk over to the brazier, not without drawing attention. So, the obvious--and tricky--solution is to light something on fire and toss it inside from a distance.

He trusts his aim, suboptimal conditions or not. The darkness isn't too much of a hindrance; a skylight over the brazier allows in just enough of the weak Evernight light to illuminate its metallic exterior. By his estimate, it's about fifty meters away, which his practiced arm can easily reach, so long as he has something solid to throw.

In his safe room, he found a crate of prepared torch heads, dusty but still functional. He's not sure what exactly constitutes them, but whatever tar is in the center of the cloth covering is weighty, and makes it excellent for this task. He fishes out the one he stowed in his bag along with the flint.

There's no use in hesitating. Striking the flint against a sharp edge of his gauntlet casts a shower of sparks across the torch head, which begins to smolder after some gentle exhales against its surface. He waits until a proper flame takes root--and not a second later--before cocking his arm back and sending the fireball sailing through the air, aim true, to land square in the brazier.

Much like insects, Titankin are drawn to the alluring glow of fire, seeking both its light and motion in darkness. As the flames in the brazier steadily grow, the beasts march from all corners of the room to the center to crowd around it.

And in the wavering light, with minds degraded by the Black Tide and many thousands of years of waiting, it takes very little for a packed crowd of Titankin to turn on each other. A sword pokes a back, a foot stomps on another, a fist knocks into a chest, and suddenly, everything is an enemy. Violence is slow to overtake the group, but confusion and the eagerness to fight after so much dormancy win out eventually. Soon enough, their blades cut friends like foe with the same programmed brutality. Ichor spills across the floor, gleaming in the firelight like molten gold. The cacophony of battle echoes up to the ceiling as prayers once did within these hallowed walls.

All Mydei needs to do is spectate, completely silent and still, making sure that no Titankin sees him as a target. Participation would be more interesting, but in these circumstances, he's perfectly fine with watching Nikador's creations reduce themselves to rubble.

He's not sure how long it takes for the bloodbath to end. The brazier still burns bright once silence overtakes the temple once more, revealing a mess of carnage across the floor and the last few stragglers--the victors. Mydei, of course, is the real victor, and he finishes them off in a few decisive strikes.

A satisfied smile tugs at his lips. That plan worked out even better than he could've imagined, and a glance at his pocket watch informs him that it's not even action hour yet.

He turns to the entryway, ready to return to the safe room--and instantly freezes.

Somebody's approaching. Quickly approaching.

"--Hello? Who's there?" the person shouts, and gods, oh dear gods, it's Phainon. Mydei scrambles back into the side hallway and locks himself in place, unwilling to attempt an escape when he could so easily be heard. He should be safe here; the brazier's light doesn't make it to this corner, and the acrid smoke covers up whatever traces of his scent he's left.

Of course, none of that will help if Phainon begins a thorough search.

"Hello? Hello?"

His voice is getting louder. He'll be in the central room in seconds. Damnit, why is he back in Janusopolis again? The others should be searching for him elsewhere, they must've ruled out this area by now. Was he just passing through the city when he saw the brazier light up? The temple is elevated and open to the outside on one end, it might be visible from miles away-- and godsdamnit, why didn't Mydei consider that risk?

It's too late. There's no point in regretting the mistakes he's already made.

Mydei hears the entryway doors slam open. A moment later, Phainon appears from the darkness, sprinting full-speed toward the brazier. The vast room feels infinitely smaller now. Closer and closer he draws, millisecond by millisecond. Time itself seems to slow. Adrenaline burns through Mydei's limbs like wildfire. A hand rests atop his abdomen, guarding the secret he may have failed to keep.

Is it over?

"Hello, who's--what in the--"

Before Phainon can finish his question, he trips on a Titankin's corpse.

It's not a terrible fall; he knows not to break it with his hands and lets himself land on his chest instead. Mydei hears his breath get knocked out in a loud gasp. And that should be the worst of it, beside some possible bruising later on.

He's fine, he shouldn't even be phased.

But he doesn't get up.

Instead, he slowly drags his knees under himself and braces his forearms against the ground, putting him in a low hunch. He remains there at the foot of the brazier, trembling slightly, heaving for air. His breaths start to sound shaky, then hitching, and he's suddenly sobbing.

One arm raises enough for him to slam his fist against the ground. "... Godsdamnit... I'm so... I'm so fucking useless, I can't do it, I can't fucking do it..."

Mydei grits his teeth.

"... Mydei... I'm so--... so fucking s-sorry," he chokes out, barely able to speak through his sobs, "I failed you... failed and... should've..."

Again, his fist slams down. This time, the tile cracks.

"I love you so much, please--"

An inhale so rough he gags--

"--come back, I'll explain everything, I didn't mean to scare you, I love--"

Slam--

"--both of you--"

And Mydei's world stills.

Both of you?

He must've misheard. Phainon doesn't know, he can't know. He must mean something else.

Mydei's ears strain, waiting for more, anything to save him from the precipice of collapse.

The fire crackles, and Phainon just sobs, choking on air, broken and raw, a heap of white on the dirty ground, Titankin ichor soaking into his sleeves and staining his hands, face smeared with tears and snot, reduced from a Deliverer to a man, just a man, desperately begging for what he's lost.

Mydei can't breathe. It's too terrible, and it's his fault, all of this suffering wrought for a lie that may have been pointless.

"... Our child... I failed you, too."

And there it is.

Phainon knows.

What is there left to do?

Perhaps he should just step out and end this farce. It's a terrifying thought. To face Phainon now--he doesn't think he can bear it. What he wants to do is run, hide, bury himself in the ground so he doesn't have to face the consequences of this terrible and meaningless thing he's done to the person he loves so dearly.

But he isn't afforded a choice. The universe makes one for him, because from the darkness a furiae praetor emerges, presumably alerted by Phainon's noisiness or the burning brazier. Phainon himself is unaware of its approach, still hunched over and lost in his own grief.

Its sword begins to rise, prepared to fall upon Phainon's unguarded back.

Mydei leaps forward to meet it.

In bounding strides, he crosses the room, reaching the praetor in a second. His forearms brace together, raised to catch the broadsword's downswing-- the crash is deafening, the blow forceful enough to crack the blade and send Mydei skidding backwards.

Phainon makes a sound behind him, some sort of strangled gasp caught in a sob. Mydei forces himself to ignore him and begins his assault upon the Titankin, lunging forward to strike its body. It blocks with its free arm; the entire forearm is blasted off from the force, but it seems unbothered by the loss.

Its broadsword swings again, this time at Mydei. He ducks under and dives to its backside, aiming an uppercut at the vulnerable junction between its legs. Unlike a living creature, it has no sensitive organs there, but it's still a good way to throw it off-balance. It stumbles, barely managing to remain upright, and Mydei strikes again, fist punching through its lower back. He lingers inside for a moment to send a burst of crystal out from his palm, shredding through its internal stone structures.

Of course, such a large Titankin can't be felled with just one hit. When Mydei yanks his hand free, the gush of ichor that follows isn't nearly enough to bleed it dry. He manages another strike at its upper back before he has to dodge, easily sidestepping the slanted arc of the broadsword. As it attempts to recover, he takes the opportunity to kick at one of its legs; he doesn't anticipate it falling, but it seems he nailed it at the right angle.

Cracks streak across its body as it slams against the ground. He stomps through its back with one foot, and it fully shatters, the broken pieces of its body and its lifeblood joining the carnage of its comrades around it.

But Mydei isn't looking at it anymore.

Phainon has risen from his hunch. His eyes are no longer downcast; he stares up at Mydei with a slack jaw as if he's one of the Titans themselves descended from the heavens, shock and awe and something unreadable all mixing together in his expression.

The distance between them is less than ten meters, but Mydei cannot force himself to cross it. He can't move at all, even when Phainon gets to his feet and the wild part of his mind once again screams at him to run.

But Mydei doesn't want to run anymore. Under the stink of ichor and coal, he can smell Phainon, and he knows he's home.

He counts the paces that Phainon takes to reach him, keeping his gaze fixed at his approaching boots instead of his face. Footsteps ring in his ears. And then, those boots are right in front of him, and he has to look up, look into those searing blue eyes, look at that beautiful face he's missed so dearly.

"... Mydei," Phainon whispers, almost as if he's afraid. A hand darts out tentatively, and Mydei doesn't shy away as it rests upon his left shoulder. He's wearing his himation, but through the thick fabric, he can feel the heat of his palm.

"You're here, you're okay."

And something about the way he says it, with so much care, like nothing else in the world matters--it finally breaks the dam. Mydei grabs him and Phainon's grabbing him back, two sets of arms desperately tangling and squeezing them together so tightly it hurts, but neither of them try to pull away. Phainon's face is buried in the side of his neck; Mydei feels his shuddering inhale against his own chest.

"Phainon, I'm sorry," he manages, eyes burning with tears he'll never be able to shed, "I shouldn't have left."

"Don't apologize, it's not your fault. I should've... done it all differently," he chokes out. "I made you think... Titans, I don't know what I made you think, exactly, but you thought I wouldn't care for them--for our child."

I was just so scared to lose you, he wants to explain, but it lodges in the back of his throat. He still can't say what matters most.

"You said you didn't want to have a family with me," is what he says instead. It sounds accusatory and he hates it. He can only hope that Phainon will read between the lines like he always has in the past.

Because how could Mydei risk losing the one person who has dealt with him, in all his bluntness and stubbornness and roughness, and loved him not in spite of it, but because of it? However small that chance might've been-- how impossible it really was--he couldn't allow it.

And gods, does he know how stupid it was. It's hard to feel relief when the guilt is busy gnawing a hole through his heart.

"I was afraid back then, just afraid," Phainon shakily assures him, "I wouldn't have been angry, and I'm certainly not angry now, not about our child. I can't say I'm not upset with you for not telling me, but... I think I understand why you did, and I'm sorry."

"... You know I trust you. The blame doesn't lie with you," he murmurs.

Phainon sniffles, and hugs him a bit tighter. "I don't want to blame you, either. The world has been so cruel to you. I want to be at least one good part of it, if you'll let me. Just tell me when you're hurting and I'll help you, always."

"Even when I make it difficult?"

"Of course," he insists, "loving you is never difficult. You're the easiest person in the world to love, Mydeimos."

And Mydei doesn't have another argument left. They'll need to talk about this more, so much more, but he can't, not right now. The adrenaline's worn off and exhaustion has settled not just in his bones but his mind. Discussing consequential matters is beyond him.

So, he kisses Phainon instead, slow and gentle. It has been far too long since the last one and Mydei can only regret the wait. He melts into the touch, the warmth and wetness of it, the realness of Phainon's mouth against his own, and Phainon eagerly accepts him.

It feels just as it did before, not stilted or forced. Their bond remains strong, shaken but not irreparably, and what a comfort it is to know that, despite all his terrible flaws, Phainon will still love him the same. Perhaps he doesn't deserve such forgiveness--he feels that he doesn't--but he's selfish enough to accept it.

Phainon deepens the kiss. Mydei wants to reciprocate, but a part of him, newly awakened by hormones, aches for so much more; going further will ruin him, and he knows he shouldn't. Instead, he pulls back to breathe, though he slots their fingers together as a promise, assuring him that there won't be any more running.

"Let's go back to Okhema."

In the darkness, Phainon's smile shines as bright as the blazing sun.

They stop by Mydei's safe room first to gather his things. Phainon helps, though not much, as he keeps stopping to stare at him and the surroundings. Mydei doesn't care enough to berate him; it's not as if he has much to pack, the lack of aid is inconsequential. Phainon does insist on carrying his bag, which Mydei allows without protest.

It's clear that he has something else to say, but he doesn't voice it until they're well on their way back to Okhema.

"Do your feet hurt, or your legs?" he first asks, a bit awkwardly.

"Not enough to bother me."

"You're certain? We can slow our pace if you want, I don't mind. I'll even carry you."

Mydei can only sigh at Phainon's pleading, wide-eyed stare; he'd be frustrated if anybody else was so persistent, but somehow, he finds this all quite endearing.

"It really is fine," he insists. "I only care about reaching Okhema as quickly as possible."

"Okay... I just want to take care of you, and I know being pregnant is hard..."

"It isn't so taxing for me. I must imagine that my body lessens the strain, just as it eases my other aches and pains. On that front, there isn't much to be done."

A pause.

"You were going to spend the whole pregnancy out here, weren't you? And you were going to give birth alone?"

The sudden question catches him off-guard, so much so that he almost refuses to answer. But he considers it for a moment, and decides to offer a nod, nothing more, to let Phainon process it on his own.

They lapse into comfortable-enough silence, though for the rest of the journey back, Mydei's expecting him to say something else on the matter. He doesn't, and his mouth stays shut until they're approaching the city gates, when one of the guards--Mydei recognizes him as Kebes, one of the younger Kremnoans--breaks from his post to run toward them.

"Prince Mydeimos! You're back!" he cries. His youth combined with the amount of time spent in Okhema means he's not very stoic, and his discipline is somewhat lacking, though Mydei has no current desire to scold him. Just this once, it's fair to let it slide.

"Indeed, all thanks to the Deliverer himself."

"All thanks? There's no need to be facetious," Phainon protests.

"I'm being serious, though I'll take it back if you don't believe me."

Kebes laughs in delight. "I see you're both in good spirits! What excellent news this is! I'll go tell the Kremnoans, we must throw a feast to celebrate your return, perhaps even a festival."

"I appreciate the enthusiasm, but you must attend to your post. I'll see the Kremnoans myself."

"Ah, of course, of course..."

Mydei bids the young guard farewell, and he and Phainon pass through the gates into the city proper. A month is not a particularly long time to be away, but it feels as if eons have passed since he last walked through these streets. The hustle and bustle of ordinary life is just as it was before, and oddly enough, he finds that all the noise lifts his spirits.

The noise only increases as they pass, citizens pointing and chattering and brandishing their teleslates to photograph. Mydei gives a few awkward waves because Phainon insists, saying it will reassure them that all is well, though he's not sure his appearance is in any way reassuring. From the few glimpses of himself he's gotten in mirrors scattered about Janusopolis, he looks very much like a man that's been living in the wild.

He can only imagine how much of a stir his disappearance caused, and his return will only fuel more speculation. If the people's curiosity is to be sated, he'll have to come up with a good story, one that divulges just enough truth to keep it believable while keeping his own turmoil private. It's a tall order, but a necessary one. An unfortunate part of being a Chrysos Heir is that he must manage his image, lest he make the others of his rank look bad.

He can work it out later. His mind is too fried to conjure up that good story, or anything else, really. He'd love to march right back to his chambers and fall asleep within Phainon's embrace, but that will have to wait.

"Go tell Lady Aglaea that I'm back. I'll join you shortly, I just have to speak with Krateros first."

Phainon nods. "I believe she's at the Mamoreal Palace, but if not, I'll send you the meeting place... Do you have your teleslate with you?"

"I believe it's in my bag. Hand it over, let me check."

Mydei spent so much time with a non-functioning teleslate, stuck outside of the reaches of Aglaea's threads, that he almost forgot it existed. Indeed, it is buried at the bottom of his bag, almost out of charge, but with enough to make it to the end of the day, so long as he checks it sparingly. He ignores the wall of missed messages that greet him and pockets it before embarking on his mission to find Krateros.

At this hour, he's certain his master will be supervising the training grounds, and he's correct. He's leaning against a wall, arms crossed, watching as a line of soldiers practice footwork drills. His expression is as impassive as ever, until he notices Mydei's approach, of course.

"Young lord, you--!" He nearly chokes on his own words, and pauses to clear his throat forcefully, continuing with a bit more restraint. "You've returned to Okhema, I see. Welcome back, I'm pleased to see you in... what I hope is good health."

Mydei unconsciously reaches up to comb through his hair, cringing when his fingers catch on thick tangles. "I'm well. I haven't had access to a proper bath in a while, so excuse my appearance. Coming to see you felt more important than freshening up."

"It matters little to me, I only care to know where in the world you went."

"I was in Janusopolis of my own volition. Though it pains me to admit, I must confess that I was hiding... though not without reason. There is something I must tell you, if we can go somewhere more secluded."

Krateros turns to the soldiers, still practicing away and unaware of Mydei's presence. "Stand down, our prince has returned! You're dismissed for the day, vacate the training grounds posthaste."

Perhaps due to the fact that they're under the watchful eye of Krateros, the soldiers do not crowd around him, and obediently file out, though Mydei picks up their excited comments. The news will be spread through the entire district within a quint. He can already imagine the feast they'll throw in celebration; it will be a welcome affair to see his people so joyful.

He's confident that they did well without him, but he can't help but wonder exactly how well. Since the Kremnoan detachment was formed around him, he's always worried for them, as a prince and a person both. After all, there is much more to leadership than the diplomacy he carries out with the Council or his general commands. The detachment is far more than an army, it is a group of refugees foremost, and as well established as they may be in Okhema, prejudice haunts them still.

Over millennia, the Kremnoans have had a diverse line of rulers, an unfortunate number of them being infamous for their cruelty, so much so that cruel is the adjective most often associated with his people. Mydei's aware that his own efforts are little more than a drop in the ocean--culture and the perception of it are both difficult to change--but that doesn't stop him from trying to lead with kindness. He's learned enough history to recognize that, in the long run, it is much better to be loved than feared.

"What do you wish to discuss?" Krateros asks, tearing Mydei away from his thoughts. His voice and expression have softened, just enough to encourage some vulnerability.

"It is a somewhat complicated situation, and I hope you understand that I don't wish to divulge every detail. What matters most is that... Well, I am with child."

"You are--!"

Again, he clears his throat. "By Nikador, you've brought much excitement to my day. A child! What a blessing, indeed. How long until their birth?"

"I have recently passed the fifth month."

Without the himation on, Krateros could've likely discerned that himself. His pregnancy is obvious in his regular clothing worn underneath it, but not severe enough to make a bump in the heavy fabric.

"And this child was conceived from the union between you and Lord Phainon, yes?" he asks, then continues without waiting for an answer. "Perhaps I should've anticipated such an outcome. You two have already devoted yourselves to each other, and strife has strengthened your bond over the years... All the greatest rulers of Kremnos have done the same.

"But you seem so troubled, young lord. Does this outcome not please you?"

"It isn't the child that troubles me--I am happy to bear them. It is the fact of fatherhood, the burden of having a family, the... the fear of what may come. I know you've long insisted I look past such worries, especially ones so trivial, but I couldn't. Instead, I took the coward's path, and fled."

The admission brings him much shame, and he expects Krateros's ire to be mercilessly brought upon him. However, no fury overtakes his master's expression--no, a great sadness does instead, one so profound that Mydei can only wait for him to finally break the long stretch of silence between them.

His voice is rough when he finally speaks. "Mydeimos, my boy... The things you have suffered in your short life are well beyond what I can fathom. It is partially my own fault that you were ripped from your mother's arms before you were even weaned--that such unimaginable cruelty was wrought upon a babe. And when you were liberated from the sea, I placed the charge of patricide upon your shoulders before your first decade of life. You couldn't have a normal childhood, despite your mother's wish for you to know peace... I failed her, in many ways, and I failed you.

"To think that somebody like you could ever be expected to forget their fear would be stupid, and I am no fool. You are braver than I have ever been, perhaps than any Kremnoan has ever been, in spite of all that darkness you face.

"If I were to call you a coward for fleeing, then so am I. Do you believe me to be one?"

"... No, I do not. You have always been brave in my eyes."

"Then you are brave too, and I cast no judgement upon you. Did you err? Perhaps, but you have returned, and your actions prove your determination to make things right. That is all I have to say on the matter, beyond my congratulations for you and your mate. It pleases me greatly to know you'll have a family soon. Our people will certainly be overjoyed."

"Please do not inform them yet, I'd like to make a proper announcement myself," Mydei hurries to say.

And just like that, the tension dissipates. "You think I have loose lips? Hmph, of course none shall know unless you give the word, that goes without saying."

"The confirmation is only for my own peace of mind, I don't wish to butt heads with you. I've always seen you as a reliable confidant."

"As you should. Now, if this matter is settled, you should be off. I'm certain your mate wishes to spend time with you," he says, with a slight smile.

"You seem to have developed some fondness for Lord Phainon. You've always said he wastes my time, at least in the past."

Krateros breaks eye contact for a fraction of a second, almost as if he's embarrassed. "Ah, that was all a test to ensure you really were dedicated to him. A future king cannot pick their consort in haste. I'm quite certain now that you've chosen correctly, and he has proven himself worthy to stand beside you--his possessiveness over you is a very strong attribute."

"Possessive? I would not describe him as such."

"He's always by your side, is he not? He knows himself that he is the only one fit for that role, and he takes it seriously. Now, off you go, don't waste any more time. Your heart and body must both be awaiting his own."

"It's unnecessary to phrase it like that," Mydei mutters, feeling his face heat up. "But if you insist, I shall take my leave."

Despite Krateros's parting words, Mydei does not get to spend much time at all with Phainon for the rest of the day. They meet with Aglaea together, but Phainon says very little the whole time, as she's much more interested in asking Mydei questions. She tries to keep it brief, though the nature of such a meeting means it unfortunately runs for two quints, and she only ends it because he begins to have trouble keeping his eyes open.

"I must apologize," he mutters, while rubbing his hands across his face. "I don't wish to insinuate I'm bored by our conversation."

"I should apologize for exhausting you. I'll be more considerate of your pregnancy going forward. I can't guarantee there won't be any more meetings with the council--even the Titans don't have the power to prevent those--but I'll lighten your workload. Make sure to get plenty of rest."

"... Thank you, Lady Aglaea."

Phainon takes him right to his own chambers after that, per Mydei's request. He wants to lie in a bed that smells like his alpha, preferably with his alpha, but Phainon doesn't have the time to spare.

"I'll be back by curtain-fall hour, I swear it. I've just got to talk to Castorice, and return these supplies... and help Theodoros since I did promise to do that before I dropped everything to go find you... and--"

"Just go do it, the less time you spend explaining the sooner you can return."

In the face of his impatience, Phainon all but sprints from the room with a rushed apology halfway off his lips. Mydei locks the door behind him, then turns to look at his room; somehow, it has gotten even messier since he last saw it. Books are piled up in the corners and his desk is heaped with scrolls. Mydei nearly trips on a massive, rolled-up map of Amphoreus left at the foot of the bed as he tries to make his way to the washroom.

The washroom itself, at least, is tidy. It's actually a bit sparse, as it always has been. Phainon doesn't have a varied collection of soaps and oils, which Mydei has spent much of their relationship lamenting. After spending the night in your chambers, how am I meant to make myself presentable with only pine tar soap--that was his most common complaint, repeated until he finally got him to buy some proper hair products and moisturizer, though with only one choice for each.

It's better than nothing, and certainly enough for a proper bath. To wash in hot water again after so many dips in that cold creek is an almost unbelievable experience. He delights in scrubbing every centimeter of his body and carefully detangling his hair, uncaring of how long it takes.

The child seems to enjoy it too, since they actually cease their squirming for once, at least until he exits the tub. As he towels himself off, they start back up, and he can only sigh. He's so exhausted that he reckons he'll be able to sleep in spite of the disturbance.

Before he slips into Phainon's bed, he considers redressing, but decides against it. He wants to have the scent-soaked linens against his bare skin; hopefully, it will help to appease his instincts. Regardless, all his clean clothes are in his own chambers, and he's not interested in making the trip over, no matter how short.

So, he curls up underneath the sheets, pressing the upper edge of them against his nose as he drifts off to fill it with Phainon's scent, so fresh and strong and comforting. No other alpha has the same softness to theirs, that gentle undertone that has always caused Mydei to relax, unconsciously, into its embrace.

He's gone in an instant, lulled into a deep and dreamless sleep, though not so deep that he doesn't stir when the door is unlocked. Unsure of how much time has passed, he blinks his eyes open to watch Phainon step inside.

"I was trying to be quiet, did I wake you?" he asks, sheepish.

"You did, but it's alright," he says, then almost without thinking, continues, "I wished to speak with you anyway."

He can keep putting it off, but why not do it now? If he keeps waiting for a better time, then he may just keep running until it catches up with him for good.

So, in the comfort of a soft bed, with his lover beside him, Mydei finally begins to explain. His fears and doubts are laid bare, the things that drove him away, the darkness that has haunted him since his earliest memories of the sea, the story of the prophecy that doomed him at birth. Phainon knows some of it, but not all of it, not the sordid depths that until this point Mydei has preferred to ignore. He no longer wishes to pretend it doesn't affect him--if it didn't, he wouldn't have fled.

And that was the culmination of it all: his plan to birth the child in secret and return with them, and to raise them under the guise of them being an orphaned babe found out in the Evernight, thus preventing Phainon from feeling obligated to do anything.

It brings him great shame to say it aloud to the very person it insults, but he knows he must. Even if he didn't intend for it to cause harm, that doesn't change the reality of what happened, and he cannot take away the pain he made Phainon feel.

Phainon doesn't hold it against him. He seems eager to clear up every misunderstanding, explaining why he himself was so afraid of fatherhood, and why he chose avoidance over confrontation. When he speaks of the obsession that overtook him upon Mydei's disappearance, he reveals how he learned of the child he'd sired, how their bond ran so deep it ensnared their biology. Again, Mydei realizes he never had anything to fear; he isn't sure when his regret will fade, if ever.

Now, at least, the wounds can begin to heal. Once all is said, the relief is far stronger than any guilt, and Mydei basks in it.

All is said, perhaps, except for one thing.

"Let me see you, Mydei," Phainon says quietly, breaking the brief silence that had settled between them. Their entire conversation was conducted with Mydei still lying beneath the sheets and Phainon seated beside him on the edge of the mattress, and he hovers over him now, expression pleading.

It should be a simple request. Mydei can't recall ever feeling self-conscious in his life, at least over his physique. Perhaps when he was a teenager and was awkwardly growing into his body there was a bit of discontentment, but he had far greater troubles than his lankiness or oily skin, and he quickly stopped caring.

But now, a new part of him worries that Phainon won't like what he sees, that he'll feel disgust at the softness of his body in his chest and hips, and the swell of his once-rigid abdomen. He knows he shouldn't be, but he hesitates anyway, leaving the sheets still drawn up, and Phainon notices, as he always does.

"What's wrong?"

"My body, it's... different," he says stupidly, because of course it is.

"You know I don't care, I'll think you're beautiful no matter how you look. And I know you're beautiful right now. You don't have to show me yet, but--"

Mydei pulls the sheets down. He watches Phainon expression change to something unreadable as his eyes wander across his exposed skin, repressing the urge to shiver. He doesn't think he's being scrutinized, but it almost feels like it, until Phainon's hands reach to trail down his sides, and he knows with certainty that he's being worshipped.

He's so careful with his touches, as if he fears Mydei might vanish. Even when he moves to straddle him, seated atop his thighs, his fingers continue their delicate mapping, making no move to do anything else. The only place he lingers is atop his abdomen, where he places both palms flat to cradle its swell, and Mydei feels as if he can't breathe.

"Have they moved yet?" he asks, voice shaky. He's crying, Mydei realizes belatedly, and he reaches up to wipe the tears rolling down his cheeks.

"They seem to move at all hours, but they're still right now. Perhaps you soothed them," he replies quietly.

Phainon laughs wetly. "Of course they're so active, of course our ch-child... they're... Gods, I can't... I can't believe we're having a baby, Mydei. I love you so much."

"Are you going to be this sappy for the entire pregnancy?"

"Yes, I can't help it. You're so perfect, you deserve all the affection I can possibly give you. I'll make up for all the time we lost."

Mydei grabs his shirt collar and yanks him down for a desperate kiss, and holds him there until his chest burns. Phainon is the one to break it, gasping for air, a pathetic whine building in his throat, one muffled by Mydei's lips when he grabs the back of his head and pulls him in again.

"Then make up for it," he pants, "show me how good you can be. Give it all to me."

Despite his earlier plans, neither of them end up getting much sleep that curtain-fall hour.

Settling back into the routine of ordinary life is remarkably easy.

To have Mydei around again feels so natural that Phainon isn't at all disoriented when he wakes up next to him each morning. No matter the positions they fall asleep in, they always end up in a tangle, clinging with arms and legs, sharing in warmth and scent. The alpha in him is perfectly satisfied; the rest of him is delighted. Mydei's back, and the world is right once more.

Perhaps the only thing that's changed is how tightly Phainon holds onto him in those sleepy moments of dawn. He isn't something to be taken for granted. Everything in life is fleeting, but by the gods is Phainon going to try to make this last forever, in whatever way he can.

Their schedules are busy, even busier than before, but they still make time for each other. They sit together in shared meetings and read over Council decrees side by side. They train--only after Mydei assures him the exertion is not harmful--and get lunch when they have the time for it. They go on walks through the city and speak with passerbys as the day winds down.

All is as it once was--almost, anyway, because there is one glaring difference that is quite disorienting.

Phainon never truly imagined himself as a father; beyond the fear it brought him, he never thought he'd have the opportunity. Warriors as prolific as himself don't think of much beyond their duty. His body is branded with the gold of Flamechase, longing for the peace he was born into yet knowing battle much more intimately. It was always his destiny, he thought, to cast aside his own desires, his own self, to become a vessel for the world's hope.

But now, Mydei is pregnant. It's an unimaginable truth that cannot be denied. Phainon looks at him and can't possibly ignore the growing swell of his abdomen, can't ignore the faintest tap-tap-tap against his palms when he rests them against it, can't ignore the way Mydei instinctively guards it with his hands because he knows there's something inside to protect--and it's too much. Fatherhood is barreling towards them, and Mydei seems so well-adjusted while Phainon feels like he's drowning.

They're going to have a child. A precious, fragile life that is theirs to cherish. Phainon loves both them and their father so much that he wonders if his heart might collapse from the weight of it.

When they're apart, he worries. Every rational part of him knows that Mydei is more than capable of taking care of himself, but there's another part of him, something deeper and primal, that aches with fear. Once they part in the mornings, only the sight of Mydei, not even his scent, are enough to appease him. So, Phainon copes with this issue by not really coping at all, and instead drags Mydei to the baths as early in the evening as he can. He gets away with it, somehow. The mild waters in the Heroes' baths are safe for the babe, and Mydei occasionally mentions his aching joints, so the frequent trips are amenable to them both. They can spend parting hour just as they used to, lounging side-by-side and recounting the events of the day.

It is a week later, during one of these baths, that Mydei brings up the feast.

"The Kremnoans are hosting a celebration three days from now," he says, with his eyes still closed, as if he's half-asleep. Phainon, who was half-asleep, startles at his words.

"Uh... yeah, a celebration..." he mumbles, cutting himself off with a yawn. He really wants to pay attention to what Mydei's saying, but he's so pleasantly warm and sleepy, he might just drift back off--

"I'd like you to attend it with me. It's time I officially proclaim you as my partner and announce our coming child."

"Time to--but aren't you keeping them a secret?"

Though Mydei never explicitly mentioned any plan to hide the pregnancy, he's continued to wear a himation over his usual garb, so Phainon didn't know what to think. He's been meaning to ask, but he's been so busy, and so fixated on other matters, that it has continually slipped his mind.

"I have been, but it has been a month since the quickening, which means it's now the customary time to tell family and friends. Do you know anything about Kremnoan culture?" Mydei asks, cracking one eye open to glare at him.

"I do, you know I do! I just never researched anything in this particular area, since I never imagined it'd apply to me. I assumed you were hiding it so the Council wouldn't find out... which I feel seems fair. We both agreed we'd keep our relationship private for the same reason."

Through a rather unfortunate incident in the baths and Phainon accidentally running his mouth while tipsy, the other Chrysos Heirs know that they're lovers, but the general populace remains in the dark. He's heard plenty of speculation over the years, though with no hard evidence, the rumors have remained quiet enough to be ignored. It was never his preference to hide something like this--he's found it difficult to not proclaim his love from the rooftops--but it seemed to be Mydei's preference, and Phainon would do anything for him. If he wants to let the world know, he'll find no resistance from his lover.

Mydei shrugs in response to his words, sending ripples across the water's quiet surface. "They'll be bothersome, but they always are. It makes no difference to me. It is the right of my people to know of their heir... and royal consort, I suppose that's what you are... which is far more important than anything else. Do you not agree?"

"No, of course I agree. I've been wanting to tell other people myself, but I was waiting for your permission. After all, it's your body, at the end of the day. You're going to be the one getting all the attention once word spreads."

"Whatever form that attention takes, I can certainly handle it."

Phainon leans to the side enough to comfortably slip his arm across Mydei's shoulder, mostly as a reassurance for himself. "I'm sure you can, but let me know if anybody bothers you too much. You know I'll take care of them."

"Hmph, you really are protective, aren't you," he scoffs, with a fond smile.

"How could I not be? I love you, and you're carrying our child right now-- there is much to be protected. You're the strongest person I've ever met, but even you are fallible. I'll always be here to watch your back if you stumble."

Mydei's features, already pink from the bath, flush darker, and he quickly looks away. Statements which feel so common to Phainon can be the things to fluster him the most. Usually, it's the cultural divide; it has never served as a real hindrance, but some words don't have the intended effect. This time, at least, Phainon doesn't see any issues with the results.

"You never answered my request. Will you come to the celebration or not?"

He accepts the change in subject without protest. "I certainly will--I wouldn't miss it for the world. Just tell me the time, I'll make sure my schedule's clear."

"The festivities will begin at the commencement of action hour. We'll go to the mess hall together, I need to ensure you're dressed properly beforehand. Only the Fates know what sort of outfit you'd conjure up if left to your own devices."

"If you insist," he says, knowing he doesn't have much of a defense. Aglaea's either designed or approved most of the clothes in his wardrobe, so he doesn't think he can make a fool of himself anymore, and yet he still isn't trusted.

Mydei seems content with his response, and they lapse back into silence once more; however, Phainon's mind doesn't quiet back down.

They'll be announcing their relationship in three short days. Gods, what will everyone think? He doesn't care much for their opinions of himself, but of Mydei, he cares much more. There are plenty of people who look down upon pregnant, unmated omegas--as if the alpha or beta doesn't share just as much responsibility--and that compounds upon the existing contempt for Kremnoans. It's impossible to not worry about what sort of hatred will be lobbed his way.

Is there anything Phainon can do to prevent at least some of it? Of course, there certainly is, and it's something he's wanted to do since he and Mydei first laid together, before their relationship was defined and was instead a strange friendship with stilted, desperate tangles after sparring, when neither of them knew what to do about the tension that simmered between them, as two people so unexperienced in matters of romance. Phainon would look at the tantalizing skin on the sides of his neck and imagine, but he never acted. In the beginning, it wasn't realistic to dream of such a thing, and now--he doesn't know.

Is now the time to broach such a topic? Perhaps not, but if he keeps putting it off he'll never end up doing it, and that sounds worse than the alternative.

As they prepare for bed, he finally decides he'll ask.

"Do you think the Kremnoans will judge us?"

The moment the question leaves his mouth, he regrets it. Could he at least have waited until tomorrow, when he'll be dressed properly instead of wearing nothing but his boxers with little seals on them? Well, it's too late to take it back.

Mydei pauses in the middle of undoing his braid. "Judge us for what?"

"Having a child without being mated."

"You worry too much," he says in lieu of an answer, and Phainon huffs.

"Just answer the question, please?"

"I think it's something you can deduce on your own, but if you insist. The perception is the same as the perception of having a child out of wedlock. And you're aware of how common marriage is between Kremnoans?"

"Almost unheard of, yes, I know."

"Then you also understand the reason. Why form a bond even stronger than marriage, one carried for the rest of one's life, when your mate may die many years before you, leaving you burdened with untreatable phantom pain? To many, the choice is obvious.

"Though times have changed since we settled in Okhema, the custom still holds. A couple only chooses to bond when their love is strong beyond measure."

"That's good, then. At least you don't have to deal with your own people judging you."

"You really do worry too much. Whatever judgement I face has no bearing on my own thoughts."

"But Mydei, you know how a lot of the Okhemans will act when they find out. You're going to get hounded and I'm supposed to, what, just watch? You shouldn't have to endure any of that nonsense, no matter how much you think you can take."

"I understand, but I can't think of what you can do beyond watching. Some things are inevitable, and I'd rather not waste time considering what-ifs. Accepting reality is far easier in the long run."

"... Do you think we could bond?"

Mydei finishes letting down his hair before he responds. Phainon watches his deft fingers, so slim and nimble without the gauntlets, comb through the loose strands.

"We could," he answers simply. "The possibility exists."

"But--but Mydei, do you really want to? I want to, I really do," he confesses, no longer able to hold back. "I want to claim you, I want you to claim me, I want to know I'm yours and you're mine forever. Not just because the world expects it, but because I love you."

"All of this questioning was just your elaborate method to ask if you could bite me, wasn't it? I should've guessed from the beginning."

"I suppose it was..."

Mydei reaches out to grab his wrist, yanking him toward the bed in one swift motion. He stumbles, half-falling onto the mattress with only Mydei to support him, and before he can even react, he's already being flipped to face the ceiling, Mydei straddling him, seated firmly on his crotch. Phainon makes a strangled sound, a bit shocked but mostly aroused, because gods how can he not be?

"Then do it."

It's a simple command, in theory. If he were any other alpha, maybe he'd know exactly what bonding entailed, but he doesn't. There must be more to it than just biting a scent gland, right? Mydei definitely wants to have sex, and that must be part of it; should he just do what he always does, or be extra romantic, or more rough, or do something unique, or--

Before he can decide, Mydei's leaning down to kiss him while grinding down with his hips, and he loses his train of thought. What remains is a steadily mounting anxiety that makes it difficult to concentrate on what should be his focus.
