In Mydei's youth, when he was a fresh rescue from the Sea of Souls and still learning to speak, Krateros would spend hours regaling him with Kremnoan legends, teaching him both language and history in one fell swoop.

One of the more interesting stories was of Queen Colubra, who ruled soon after the great King Gorgo when the kingdom of Kremnos was still in its infancy. As a young child, she--through some means--imbibed the golden blood of Nikador, granting her unparalleled strength. An unintended consequence of her skill was that no one was able to match her in a courting duel, meaning that, for many years, the people believed she would never have a consort. Her advisors requested that she take a spouse to continue Gorgo's bloodline, but she adamantly refused.

Then, on a perfectly ordinary day, Colubra vanished. The Kremnoans, as a strong and resourceful people, did not allow their society to collapse without their queen, and instated one of her guards as acting ruler while they attempted to locate her, to no avail. In fact, she did not want to be found. Ten months later, she returned upon her own volition, strolling back through the palace gates as if nothing at all had happened, cradling a newborn babe against her chest.

"I found my equal", she declared, "and sired a child with her."

The child was no ordinary child, having the ears of a fawn and a tiny set of antlers atop their head. Their mother was a forest nymph; indeed, no mortal could hope to match the strength of Queen Colubra. It was a strange outcome, but the Kremnoans were overjoyed nonetheless, and hosted a grand feast to celebrate.

Mydei always liked this particular legend. It was a celebration of life, not death, and to a child who'd experienced much of the latter, a happy ending was a novel, but welcome, reprieve. So, though it isn't a tale of much historical significance, it's always been one that Mydei has remembered.

Today, history repeats itself. He's preparing to go to a feast held to celebrate his return after an unexplained absence--and once he announces their existence, it will be celebrating Kremnos's new heir.

With the event upon him, he does find himself saddled with a bit of trepidation. Why, he can't say. The Kremnoans have always been fiercely loyal to their rulers, even to their own detriment. And that's not the problem.

It pains him to admit even to himself, but he wasn't telling Phainon the truth. He does concern himself with what the Okhemans will think. A part of him does, anyway--the covetous part of him that spends every waking moment fixated on the child.

He's never minded his secondary gender much until the past few months, when it began overwhelming him with instincts too powerful to ignore. He's sick of it, of being so unsettled. The luxury of living in the city has made him accustomed to being comfortable, something he wouldn't have been able to imagine in his youth, as being unsettled was just a fact of life.

"Uh, Mydei? I think I might've put the jewelry on wrong, can you check it for me?"

He's brought back to reality by the sound of Phainon's voice calling to him from the washroom. With less than a quint left until the feast, they're both getting dressed for the occasion. Of course, Phainon wished to wear traditional Kremnoan garb, as he insisted on being as respectful as possible. Nobody would've cared, Mydei's certain--but when he gets a proper look at Phainon, he realizes it would have been a loss had he not. Dressed in a light chiton which exposes his well-muscled physique, with a crimson drape pinned at his shoulder, and golden jewelry adorning his collar and arms, he is a sight for sore eyes.

Mydei swallows thickly. "It looks fine."

"Okay... but why are you staring at the necklace? Did I really put it on right?"

"You did, it's not the sort of thing you can put on wrong," he insists, forcing himself to look up at Phainon's eyes. "I was--ahem. I was not looking at the necklace."

"Oh, so you like it. You think I look extra handsome in these clothes... And you're the one who said it didn't matter if I dressed nicely..." he lilts in a tone that makes Mydei consider punching him.

"It's perfectly acceptable to change one's opinion when presented with new information."

Phainon slinks forward, gently pushing Mydei back against the bed. "But do you think I look good in this outfit, or would I look even better if I took it all off?"

He laughs sharply. "This is the worst attempt at seduction you've managed so far. We have to leave soon, let me finish getting ready."

While Mydei dons the last of his accessories, Phainon mopes by the window, forlornly staring off at the cityscape beneath them. Typical. He acts like a kicked chimera when he's down, though he always tries to hide it.

"My other attempts at seduction have been good, right?" he asks sadly, just as Mydei is putting on a set of rose gold earrings.

"We're mated, you fool."

"Yeah, but all my practice means I should be great at flirting by now! I'm not going to rest on my laurels, what sort of mate would that make me?"

"If you're patient, you can try some more lines on me tonight, and I have an inkling that it might work. Only after this event, though. If I can have patience, so can you."

Mydei offers him a chaste kiss to placate him before pulling him to the door. If they leave now, they'll be a fair bit early, but if they linger in the bedroom any longer, Phainon just might manage to tempt him into doing something more than a kiss. For whatever reason, they always lose their restraint around each other. As Chrysos Heirs, they are meant to be level-headed, rational, and responsible, but together, they turn into fools, racing to the bottom of the barrel. Mydei has never minded this dynamic; in fact, he relishes it. Around Phainon, he doesn't have to be anything at all.

But there is more to his life than just Phainon. He needs to keep up appearances for his people, and that means not allowing himself to be goaded into making stupid decisions, no matter how tempting they may be.

The walk to the Kremnoan district is mostly quiet. Uncharacteristically, Phainon seems to have nothing to say, in sharp contrast to his blabbering just minutes before. Mydei assumes he's finally got the memo and has decided to behave himself--an incorrect assumption, he finds, when Phainon reaches for his hand and Mydei feels how clammy his palm is. It seems the nerves have set in.

"... What if the Kremnoans suddenly decide they don't like me?" he eventually asks, confirming Mydei's suspicions. He's smiling, as if he's not being serious, but it's hollow. That question is genuine. His vulnerabilities always linger beneath the surface, never quite healing with the passage of time, just controlled well enough to keep most people from noticing the cracks.

Mydei knows how it feels. They may have lived very different lives, but the world imparted similar lessons upon them, and showed them much of the same cruelty.

"That's not going to happen," Mydei reassures him, "at this point, there are few things you could do to ruin your reputation, and being my mate is not one of them."

You are good enough, regardless of their opinions, he thinks, though he keeps it to himself. His multiple attempts to get that idea through Phainon's thick skull have failed, and he can't imagine this time will be any different.

"If you're certain."

"I always am, and it would do you well to not doubt me."

He's not sure if Phainon's fears have been assuaged, but his smile now reaches his eyes. The remainder of their walk is conducted in much more comfortable silence, fingers lightly interlocked, only separating once they reach the doors of the mess hall.

The structure was originally built inside of the Kremnoan barracks, as the very first construction project undertaken by the detachment in their Council-alloted land. It was far from luxurious--it was so cramped and unpleasant that the soldiers preferred to eat outside instead. It wasn't necessarily a problem, but when their numbers grew over the coming months, and the district developed into a proper community, Mydei realized some changes needed to be made. Not only did the mess hall go unused, but the Kremnoans moved from the barracks into houses, leaving the entire complex abandoned. They had very little land to work with, they couldn't afford this waste of space. So, he suggested that the mess hall be expanded, replacing the structure with a grand feast hall, to mirror the one in Castrum Kremnos.

It took much hard work, but with enough time and plenty of enthusiasm, the mess hall has become quite the sight. Expertly carved columns reach up to the vaulted ceilings, tapestries and war-banners adorn every wall, scones cast the room in a warm, comforting glow, and the feast table spans its length, its lacquered wood shining in the candlelight. It isn't much of a mess hall anymore, and yet, all the Kremnoans refer to it as such; nobody wishes to forget its humble beginning.

Like any mess hall, seating is not assigned. Mydei rarely chooses to sit at the table's head, even for important occasions, and today isn't the day he'll stray from his routine. He notices a young girl eyeing the king's chair as he surveys the room, and offers it to her. The Kremnoan children love to boast about who gets the seat of honor at the last feast, so she'll have bragging rights for the next few months. He can see her excitement as she hops up into the chair.

Phainon smiles at him as they go to take their own seats, with a look in his eyes Mydei can't quite name. "You're going to be such a good father."

"Don't speak of that right now, somebody could overhear us," he grouses. "I informed you how the announcement will go, and I will not allow your loose lips to ruin my plan."

His plan, in all honesty, wasn't the most well thought-out, mostly due to the fact that he chose to wear the same style of traditional chiton as Phainon. The fabric doesn't hide his pregnancy, instead accentuating it. He can only hope that the dim lighting obscures him somewhat.

"It's so loud in here, I can barely make out what you're saying, much less anybody else. But I'll do my best to keep quiet."

"I'm sure it will be an immense struggle for you."

"You think I became a debate champion by keeping my mouth shut? Being so taciturn isn't always an attribute, Mydeimos."

"... If you'd like to avoid getting thrown across the hall, you should learn some restraint."

"Don't threaten me with a good time," Phainon says, his grin sharpening. Mydei decides to ignore him, and greets the group that just sat to his left, composed of a few young warriors. He saw them earlier in the day at the training grounds, as he was running drills for the new recruits--a job he can still handle even as his pregnancy progresses, though not as frequently. Even standing around and shouting orders is enough to exhaust him.

The warriors must be wondering why he's mostly absent from the training grounds, but they don't mention it. Instead, they rush to tell him how hard they worked in the interim preceding his return. He's glad to hear it; if his weakness leads him to an early grave, the Kremnoans will not fall to ruin without their prince, they will keep pushing ahead.

And yet, as that thought crosses his mind, he shudders.

Such a thought would have previously been fleeting. Dying so many times made the whole thing feel entirely mundane. A part of him knows it's not a healthy way to think, but with his curse, he finds it hard to think any other way.

Now, even recalling the path to the Netherworld, so well-trodden by his boots, makes his stomach churn. Temporary or not, he doesn't wish to see those gates again, hear how they whisper to him, feel how they tug at him, almost tempting. To consider giving up--even if it is Death's Hand forcing that consideration into his mind--is a betrayal.

But he shouldn't be thinking about such dour things. This is an eve for celebration. His body is home to a life he dearly cherishes, and of that, the world shall know.

The influx of guests has slowed to a trickle; it's time for the feast to begin, and that means a raring speech from the prince to kick off the festivities. Usually, he feels he ends up repeating the same things at every celebration and it isn't actually raring, but that won't be the case today. He bothered to practice his speech for once--a rarity for him, since he prefers to speak from the heart.

"Is it time?" Phainon asks, noticing the shift in his demeanor.

"Yes, so long as you remember what you're meant to do."

"Stand when you say my name, of course. I'd never forget such simple instructions."

"I'd think not, but you always manage to surprise me."

Mydei doesn't linger to see if Phainon is affronted by the comment, instead pushing his chair back and rising to his feet. Immediately, the room quiets, conversation falling to hushed whispers and exclamations of excitement.

"It is a pleasure to stand before you, my people" he begins, voice easily carrying through the hall, "as it has been far too many months since we last came together in celebration. A mere week ago, you wondered why I had vanished, and if I would ever return.

"As I struggled outside the city walls, I imagined all your restless thoughts, and how you must be soldiering on in spite of them. It gave me strength--I'd return to you soon enough, I vowed. I had not anticipated that I'd find myself in such dire straits when I departed Okhema for a routine mission-- let this serve as a reminder to never underestimate the Evernight, no matter your skill.

"I fought through legions of Titankin, my every waking hour spent in vicious combat. They threatened to overwhelm me at times, so great were their numbers, but not once did I falter. When my body ached with exhaustion, when my mind went numb from the repetition of slaughter, when the chance of escape from the hordes seemed slim to none--I did not lose my determination."

The Kremnoans cheer. It does little to ease the guilt that he feels, having lied to them so blatantly. Knowing that the truth of their prince's weakness would be too much for them, he falsified a version of the events, then asked Phainon to write them into a segment of his speech. Dishonesty, no matter how kind, is far from being one of his strengths. To be frank, Phainon isn't always the greatest liar, but when it matters, he does it very well.

It seems his lie was suitable this time, and was sold by Mydei's delivery. He waits for the cheering to quiet before continuing.

"For Kremnoans, our greatest source of determination is each other. Our community is strong, and the principles of honor and virtue we follow have kept us together for millenia. With our own hands, we have forged a place for ourselves. I take great pride in every one of you, for the business, homes, and families you have built here in spite of it all.

"As your prince, I have been a spectator to your lives, to the extent that I, for many years, did not think much of my own. The work I had to do was all-consuming, and I hadn't a moment of peace for myself. But now... Seeing you all thrive in the face of hardship, I realized my work wasn't all-consuming anymore.

"Though this feast was not thrown in anticipation for any announcement, it is as good a time as any for me to make two. First, it is my great pleasure to present my mate, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae."

This round of cheering is almost deafening. Phainon's all smiles as he stands beside Mydei, shining in the face of such immediate enthusiasm. The response is just as he anticipated; most everyone loves the Deliverer, with the Kremnoans being no exception. He's helped many members of the detachment since their arrival in the city, has advocated for them despite the stigma that came with it, and--perhaps most significantly--is an extremely competent warrior.

"He has been my partner for multiple years, but until recently, I did not wish to speak about the depth of our relationship. Our bond is precious, why should I invite public scrutiny upon it? However, I've come to realize that hiding this is simply impossible. We have made a permanent promise to each other, branding skin with teeth for the world to see. If anybody wishes to judge, so be it.

"We have also made a decision even more meaningful, the consequences of which are... Even more difficult to hide. So, I have another announcement-- one that I thought I would never have the chance to make. It seems fate has spared us some kindness, and with nothing but joy in my heart, I can proclaim that I am with child."

Mydei thought he was prepared for the reaction his words would elicit. Excitement is understandable, but the celebration which erupts is so overwhelming that even he feels nervous. It's as if he proclaimed that the Era Nova was upon them.

He can't fully process what happens next; he says something to finish off his speech that he's not sure makes sense and nobody heard anyway, sits back down, and then zones out as he's bombarded by congratulations from every direction.

The thing that grounds him, some indeterminate amount of time later, is Phainon shaking his shoulder and asking him if he'd like some pomegranate juice. He gratefully accepts the offered glass before quickly emptying it.

His stomach has been touchy even with Hyacine's medicine, but at least his favorite drink remains untainted by his new sensitivities.

"You doing okay?" Phainon asks, almost having to shout over the noise, which has scarcely died down.

"I, uh, have had some conversations in the past," Phainon says, with a nervous laugh, "where I maybe said a bit too much. About myself, not you, exactly... I just found it cute how you'd play with the Kremnoan children in the square, and maybe asked some weird questions, but don't worry, I found the answers very endearing!"

"Hmm. Endearing." Mydei narrows his eyes. "How much of the concept of me wanting to have children is endearing to you? When you told me you were 'going to get me pregnant again' was that a part of--"

"Do not bring that up right now!" he cries, burying his head in his hands.

"You said yourself that nobody can overhear us in here, what's the matter?" he asks innocently, enjoying the strangled, pained sound that Phainon produces.

"It's not that, it's... Damnit... I just said it in the heat of the moment, okay? I wasn't thinking straight."

"So, you didn't mean it?"

Phainon lifts his head to give him a pleading look. "I didn't... I meant it a little, but--but no, I... Is this payback for all the times I flirted with you in the public baths?"

Mydei smirks, unable to keep up his facade. "Perhaps. I now understand why you did that, it's quite fun. Everyone can see how easy it is for me to fluster you."

"At least one of us is having fun," he sighs. "Can't we just enjoy dinner in peace?"

"We can, but you're correct, I'm not letting that comment go, so we'll be discussing it more afterward. In private this time."

He leaves Phainon to mull over his words while he turns to speak with the soldiers next to him once more, who are now offering to be a part of his child's personal guard. It's not necessary, but he thanks them for their willingness. As he's come to understand, many of them feel they owe him for what he's done, though he's never wanted anything from his people. Seeing them prosper is plenty enough.

And after an evening filled with laughter, joy, and celebration, he's more than fulfilled.

By the next entry hour, the entire city seems to have heard the news.

Upon opening his teleslate, the first thing he sees is a post about it on the world wound web, which makes him frown. Are there not more interesting going-ons than the relationships of the Chrysos Heirs? Perhaps it seems mundane from his own perspective, but even so, it doesn't make much sense to him.

He already knows he's going to get accosted if he leaves the Mamoreal Palace. Hell, he'll probably end up getting accosted here as well. The staff like to gossip just as much as everyone else.

"What have I done to upset you this time?" Phainon asks the moment he notices Mydei's discontentment. It's a solid assumption to make; he'll admit he's been a bit more sensitive for obvious reasons, and prone to being irritated by the smallest of things, like Phainon snoring too loudly, or moving too much in his sleep.

Mydei casts his teleslate aside with a sigh. "It's not you. It's the news, which you can certainly imagine. The moment I step foot out of this room, I'll be expected to explain things... as if there's anything more to explain. I said it all yesterday."

"Just stick by my side and let me field their questions," is Phainon's over-confident reply, delivered with a smile. He's so full of himself sometimes. Mydei can't resist leaning over to kiss his stupid lips.

"Don't make me look like an idiot, not like you do for yourself."

"How rude of you to insult my skills after I so kindly offered them! I declare your punishment: a trip to the baths with me, with no complaints about the early hour."

"How barbaric," he mutters. He does end up humoring Phainon, even though he's still tired enough to prefer staying in bed for at least another quint. Before his pregnancy, he'd never consider sleeping in, but it's now normal for him to forego his morning bath with his mate. Though Phainon never protested his absence, Mydei knows he's missed having him along.

Aglaea is already at the Heroes' Baths when they arrive, as always. They both strip and settle down beside her to exchange their usual pleasantries. As he already informed the Chrysos Heirs of his pregnancy a few days prior, and she knew even before that, she has little to say on the matter other than a question about how his morning sickness has been.

The announcement had gone just as he imagined it would, at least in terms of their reactions. He was aware he didn't pick the most ideal time to bring it up, as the mood in their highly important meeting was far from celebratory, but realistically, he didn't think there was a better opportunity.

In their previous discussions of Black Tide containment, he and Phainon were always on the front lines, without question. Now, they'd be stepping back--a move they couldn't make without reason. They'd discussed it already with Aglaea, and she, anticipating their decision, already had a solution in mind.

"Can you tell me why you dragged me in here?" Cipher had asked, during a lull in their discussion. She was more on edge than usual, liable to bolt from the meeting room at any moment. Mydei was surprised she accepted Aglaea's invitation in the first place.

"Aglaea invited you at my behest," Mydei said, hoping to placate her, which seemed to work. "I have a request to make of you. For at least the next few months, Phainon and I will not be able to defend the areas outside of Okhema's walls. To spare Lady Castorice from being the only Chrysos Heir tasked with such difficult work, we were hoping you could do it in our stead."

"W-what? Why?" she asked, for once appearing caught off-guard.

"I am with child, and neither of us wish to be put in any unnecessary danger."

The ensuing silence was broken, surprisingly, by Cipher's cackling laughter. "Oh my gods, I should've guessed that ages ago! No wonder you've been acting so weird! Of course! Just for satiating my curiosity, I'll pick up both your shifts--so long as Princess Homebody's there to keep me company."

"Um, I'll be there," Castorice said quietly, then with more enthusiasm, "and congratulations to you two! Please let me know if you'd like me to make anything for the baby."

"Wait, De, you're having a baby? Really?" Trianne interjected, before either of them could accept the offer.

Mydei nodded, and opened his mouth to respond, but she started cheering before he got the chance. There wasn't much hope of returning to the previous topic of conversation at that point, so he fielded a few questions before excusing himself, hoping that they might be able to get back on track with him absent.

Since then, he's spent most of his time with the Tribios and Castorice in the Garden of Life, listening to their surprisingly detailed parenting advice; upon reflection, it shouldn't be too shocking, considering their collective thousands of years of experience.

After this bath, he'll be meeting with Castorice to continue their knitting lesson, which ended prematurely due to the feast. She said he's done good work so far, and he should be able to make some simple clothes for the baby if he sticks with it, though he can't imagine that they'll be necessary, considering the amount of gifts they've already received. Between the Chrysos Heirs and the Kremnoans, they have enough supplies to swaddle a small army of infants.

Phainon would probably like it if he did choose to make something, he muses. His mate has been oddly emotional about things of that manner; perhaps some of Mydei's hormones are affecting him.

He's also been so particular about scenting him. The moment they're out of the bath, Phainon's all over him. Since their only spectator is Aglaea--who seems unbothered by almost everything--Mydei lets it happen. He himself doesn't mind some public displays of affection, at least not in theory, but Okhemans can be either very prudish or gossipy, so he's become much more reserved over the years.

Clearly, Phainon doesn't care nearly as much. He's so beloved that he can get away with anything, should he choose to go against the grain.

He pouts as Mydei begins to walk away from him, now dry and redressed. "Where are you going?"

"To the Garden of Life, I told you I was knitting with Castorice again. What, do you want to join?"

"Well, um... I don't want to be too clingy, so..."

"You are too clingy," Mydei states, which elicits a stifled laugh from Aglaea, "but I like that about you. If you want to come along, your company would be welcome, and the chimeras would be happy to see you."

"I'm not sure if I'll be any good at knitting, but I'll try if there's an extra pair of needles. With enough practice, I might be better than you, even."

"Impossible. You lack the finesse," he retorts immediately.

"I guess I'll have to surprise you, then."

They may not be able to compete on the battlefield for the foreseeable future, but it seems there's still ample room for competition in their lives.

chapters.html:
The world is burning.

Hellfire rains down upon Okhema, brought by the legions of the Black Tide. Their ranks decimated the walls and the guards with ease, almost as if they weren't there at all. Forward they marched, with relentless surety and perfect brutality, ignorant of humanity's attempts at resistance.

The stench of smoke and burning flesh mix in a nauseating perfume that fills the nose and sours the tongue. People scream for their families and children sob for their parents, all dying, all dead. The earth shakes as the city collapses, piece by piece, gilded marble and coated plaster buckling under the endless barrage. There's nowhere to run. Everywhere is fire and desecrated corpses and twisted monstrosities.

It's the end.

The Black Tide has come, and Phainon can't do anything to stop it. He never got a Coreflame, he's just a useless mortal man with ichor in his veins. A lifetime spent training, molded into a hero meant to carry the weight of the world--a waste. He failed, because he always does, because he's never going to be good enough no matter what he does.

In front of him is Mydei, collapsed to his knees, curled around a small figure he's desperately trying to protect from the coming Tide. It's a child with white hair and blue eyes and blood on their face and it's his child, he knows. Phainon can't move. Mydei's yelling at him to do something but he can't move, his feet are rooted to the ground by pillars of marble, like Kephale's own stone legs, dormant.

Gods, it's happening again. He's watching his family die in front of him and he's powerless to stop it. He knows he can't survive the grief again, it's going to break him, he's going to die too. It's not fair. None of them deserve this. None of them did anything wrong, but that doesn't seem to matter, does it? The Titans abandoned them a long, long time ago. They all knew it, but maybe, they thought, they could do it without them, and what ridiculous hubris that was, to pursue godhood. But whether they gave up or resisted-- nothing would have changed this outcome.

All he can really ask is why.

His child looks at him, with eyes a mirror of his own. They're so innocent, so precious, completely undeserving of catastrophe. He can't save them from fate. The Tide's closing it, about to consume their tiny body and Mydei too, and--

"Phainon! Open your eyes, look at me!"

Suddenly, Mydei's looming over him, very much alive and unharmed, but with a face tight with worry. Phainon makes a noise like a dying animal, a horrible rasping wail that wheezes from his lungs. One of his arms jerks forward without his input, striking Mydei on the shoulder, which feels more like hitting a solid rock wall. Mydei immediately seizes his wrist and squeezes it tight, almost too tight. Phainon struggles in his hold, though he's not sure why he wants to get away.

"Phainon, look at me," Mydei orders, and he obeys. "You're awake now, whatever happened wasn't real."

It was all a dream. It was all just a horrible fucking dream. He knows that. But he can't stop seeing it and he doesn't know how to make it go away.

Remember what Hyacine told you about flashbacks. It's the same. Ground yourself, breathe.

The sheets are soft. Mydei is warm. The room smells like soap. A lone dove sings outside. Phainon forces air into his body even though it hurts. His mouth tastes like iron. He feels like vomiting but it doesn't happen. He listens to the dove and smells the soap instead.

It takes a long time before he begins to relax. Slowly, gradually, the tension loosens, until his ribcage doesn't feel like a vice and his jaw unclenches and his eyes can properly focus on Mydei, who hasn't moved an inch and has Phainon's wrist still secured tight. He must sense that the worst of it is over, since he finally lets go. For a second, it seems like he wants to say something, but he only sighs, before clambering off to lay back down beside him.

He always knows exactly what Phainon needs, he's so kind and considerate and gentle and every other good thing that he feels like doesn't deserve. In this moment, he kind of hates it, and hates that he does. Why is he so cruel to the person who loves him the most?

"... How do you feel?" Mydei asks him quietly, after the silence between them has stretched on unbearably long. Phainon can't find an answer. Instead, he presses his palms against his eyes and weeps.

"I'm sorry," he manages to choke out. It doesn't do anything to the nauseating tangle of guilt trapped in his gut, and he's not really sure why he said it.

"Stop apologizing. Do you think I should apologize when I have nightmares? Show yourself the same grace," Mydei scolds, though not unkindly.

"I-It's too hard... I don't want to... to feel like this anymore, I hate it. It's been so many years but it still hurts so bad, it won't stop hurting and I don't understand."

"Grief is not so clear-cut. It seems to lessen over time, and yet returns anew at the strangest times. The happiest times in my life are the ones where it seems most liable to return... Why, I can't say, but it never lingers for long. It's a part of me as much as any other part, and so, I must accept it, even if I, too, wish I could be rid of it. You'll survive, just as you have, just I as have. That is life."

Mydei reaches out to cradle his cheek, and Phainon exhales shakily, doing his best to relax into the touch. His hands are so soft, protected from callouses by rapid regeneration. Phainon's are brutish in comparison, all scarred and wrinkled and a bit crooked in places from a dozen improperly healed fractures over the years.

"Do you want me to do anything for you?"

"I don't know."

"I'll get you some water, then," he replies, already heaving himself off the bed before Phainon can protest, which he does want to do. His mate is eight months pregnant and he's doing something that he could easily do himself. He knows Mydei hates to be coddled, and he's always liked to take care of others, but it's impossible not to feel guilty.

Phainon drinks the water in small sips, staring down at the cup with a furrow in his brow. He can feel the weight of Mydei's gaze on him, silently spectating. He's probably going to be like this the rest of the day, so quiet and cautious, to make sure he doesn't do something to set Phainon off. Is that worse than him being his usual self and acting like there isn't a problem? Gods, Phainon doesn't even know anymore. His thoughts are all disjointed, it'll be days before he feels like himself again.

At least neither of them have to perform their regular duties; if he had to go fight the Black Tide right now, he'd probably end up getting killed. Even the thought of having to see those disgusting beasts makes him want to vomit. He really should try to think of something else, though. This isn't making him feel any better.

"I have an appointment with Hyacine today, I'll have to go soon," Mydei says, after glancing at his teleslate, "unless you want me to stay with you."

"You didn't mention this before, is this not a prenatal appointment?" Phainon asks, immediately on edge again.

"It's not, but it's okay, nothing's the matter with the baby. Don't start panicking over nothing. I just haven't started producing colostrum yet, and she said she'd give some advice. Before you ask, I don't think you need to come along."

"I suppose I don't... But you'll tell what she tells you, if there's anything wrong or if I can do anything to stimulate production or--"

"Of course I will. By Nikador, is there anything I can do to convince you not to worry so much? I think the alpha in you has partnered up with your overbearing self to make a new sort of monster," Mydei says, sounding exasperated, though he's smiling.

Phainon manages to smile in turn. "No, unfortunately. My hormones will do what they please. But go off to your appointment, and make sure you eat something afterwards."

"As if I could ever put off eating when this child demands so much sustenance. The person I'm concerned about is you. Take care of yourself, do something to take your mind off your nightmare."

He does try. While Mydei is gone, he reads through the informational books Hyacine recommended, even though he's already read them cover to cover multiple times. He goes to get some breakfast for himself, and he's able to stomach most of it. He takes a quick soak in the baths to help clear his head a bit more, then goes back to the books to clutter it up anew. But then, two quints have passed, Mydei still hasn't returned, and he begins to worry anew.

Back in their room, he stares at his teleslate, debating just how overbearing he should be. Should he send a message asking if he'll be back soon, or call him? Mydei probably wouldn't mind the former too much, but he really does want to call--

Before he can decide, Mydei returns. Phainon's relieved until he gets a good look at him. He seems... off, in a way that's hard to pin down. If his nose were sharper, he might be able to pick up on the change in his scent, but all he can go off of is the tension in his shoulders and jaw.

"Was something the matter?" Phainon asks immediately, fearing the worst, though the logical part of his brain catches up a moment later to rationalize that, if there really was a serious problem, Mydei would be much more upset.

"What?" he replies, confused, in a manner that suggests he wasn't listening. Phainon doesn't know what to make of that. Mydei's unbelievably attentive, and he hasn't suffered from any pregnancy-induced brain fog up until this point.

"At the appointment, was anything wrong?"

"Oh, it was..." he trails off, before shaking his head. "I don't think you'll believe any lie I tell you, there's no point in trying."

Mydei sits down heavily on the bench near the window, a hand instantly moving to rest atop his pronounced bump. He's been struggling with the changes in his body, though he's not talked about it much beyond grumbling about his altered gait and center of gravity. Phainon has only seen the extent of his dissatisfaction by observation.

He considers joining Mydei on the bench to perhaps give him a massage, but opts to stay at the desk instead, after closing his book to give him his full attention.

"You shouldn't feel a need to lie," he says plainly, because it does hurt to hear, especially after all they've endured.

"I shouldn't, you're correct, but frankly, I don't believe you're in a headspace to receive troublesome news."

"Isn't it about you? You said something about milk production, right?"

Mydei sighs, while pinching the bridge of his nose with his free hand. "You're too astute of a listener for your own good."

"You can tell me right now, you've already told me enough."

"I suppose I have. But I can assure you, it's not something that needs to be said urgently, it can wait until you've had ample time to recover."

"If something's the matter with you, I want to know. I want to take care of you, no matter the state I'm in. It'll make me feel better, you know that."

"It's not something you can take care of, or anybody can."

"Really?"

"Yes. When Hyacine examined me. she determined I'm unable to lactate. My body has resisted the hormones that would have developed my breast tissue during puberty. This is apparently quite common in male omegas due to the differences in our development from females," he explains flatly, almost robotically, though he fails to hide his disappointment in his expression.

"But isn't this treatable? People can take hormones to alter their primary sex, doesn't that develop breast tissue as well?"

"It does, but..." he pauses to make a frustrated noise. "I can't take hormone treatments right now, it could harm the baby. Even if I weren't, my body may not even respond to the hormones, my immortality has altered my biology in unpredictable ways."

"Well, then we'll just feed the child formula, it's perfectly fine that you can't. I've known plenty of people of all sexes who did that for a bunch of different reasons--"

"I'm very much aware that formula exists, I'm not a fool," Mydei snaps, then immediately deflates. "I know we'll be able to feed them, I just feel as if... I've failed. My body should be able to provide for them. It is meant to be infallible, it should work."

"No part of you is infalliable, you're a human being, not a Titan. I don't like when you talk about yourself like that, it's not good for you."

Mydei makes a face. "That is quite similar to what Lady Hyacine said. It may be the truth in theory, but in practice, I have far too many burdens to bear. My people require my perfection."

"But our baby does not. They just want food, they don't care where it comes from."

He doesn't respond to that, instead breaking eye contact to look out the window. Gods, they're both so stubborn, though Phainon can't say he doesn't understand his pain. His own physical limitations have caused him much grief over the years.

"Mydei, come on, please don't beat yourself up over this. It's not what you wanted, but it's not your fault. Like you said, it's not something anybody can change, so we just have to accept it."

"Don't use my own words against me," he mutters, barely audible.

"You've told me you're always right, so..."

"If I weren't somewhat incapacitated, I'd suggest we settle this argument in the arena... but I suppose I'll acquiesce to you this once."

Phainon grins. "Hah, another win for the debate champion--"

"Don't push your luck, and don't say idiotic things until after I've given birth. It's harder to resist the urge to punch you."

"Yes, Lord Mydeimos."

He rolls his eyes. "Don't overcompensate, either. Take a nap with me and I'll forgive you."

The thought of going to sleep and risking another nightmare makes him uncomfortable, but he's tired. Mydei can certainly see it on his face and won't take no for an answer. So, they lay beside each other as they did that morning, with hopes of sweeter dreams.

"Are you alright?"

Phainon startles at the question, dropping the fork he was idly spinning onto his plate with a loud clank and making Castorice flinch.

"Perfectly so," he says automatically. She seems to believe him even less than she did the first time she asked twenty minutes ago. She invited him to this diner to have a nice chat and he hasn't been a great conversation partner; he's aware he's spent most of the meal spacing out, but he can't really help it.

"You're rather... high-strung today."

"Just thinking about the baby," he answers vaguely, hoping that explains it, because it is the truth.

The last few months of Mydei's pregnancy have been miraculously calm. He's been in perfect health and has been in relatively good spirits despite some aches and pains. There isn't anything to worry about; his immortality all but ensures that the birth will be a smooth process. Phainon isn't sure why he's so stressed other than some nebulous concern that something will go wrong. His recent nightmares have not helped in that regard.

Castorice nods sagely, understanding. "Lord Mydei is due very soon, yes?"

"Four weeks now... I can't believe it's happening so soon, I didn't think... I mean, I never thought this was going to happen in the first place, and now..."

"No matter what may happen, you're going to be an excellent father," she assures him, "so try not to fret too much. This is an exciting time!"

"Exciting is one word..." Beyond the stress, he's gotten to indulge in Mydei's heightened libido, which has only seemed to increase in the third trimester, but Castorice doesn't need to know all the details. She's put up with enough of his oversharing in the past, and he has the hindsight to recognize he's a bit too forthcoming at times.

It's hard not to think about, though. Mydei just looks so good right now, and Phainon loves to tell him all about it in all sorts of circumstances.

"Have you come up with any names? I would imagine that's quite exciting," Castorice asks, perhaps sensing that his mind is wandering away again.

"I know Mydei has. I haven't been able to think of any good names so far. I feel like he deserves the honor of naming them, anyway, since he's doing the hard work. All I've been doing is getting on his nerves by worrying all the time."

"I'm sure he's touched by your concern."

"Maybe he was at first, but definitely not anymore. I've been way too overbearing, I know I have... but Titans, these instincts I have, they're crazy. Alphas never talk about feeling this way, I don't know if it's normal or if I'm actually losing it."

Castorice hums. "Perhaps you should talk to Lady Hyacine. I can't offer you any advice, it has been hundreds of years since I felt any instincts related to my secondary sex."

"I probably should, but don't you think she's busy? I mean, whenever she comes to Okhema, she's always swamped. And I've bothered her so much these past few months..."

Unlike Mydei, Phainon has approached her with nonsensical concerns and baseless worries that she always dismisses. He cringes when he recalls the last thing he asked her, which was if they'd hurt the baby by having too much sex, the nth iteration of this same question. She was definitely fed up with having to give the same answer, he could see it in her expression.

"Well, we can go to the Twilight Courtyard just to see. It's an odd hour, there may not be too many patients waiting."

Somehow, despite his protests, they end up going. As they wait in the clinic--which is actually empty--Phainon decides he'll blame Castorice if Hyacine gets cross with him. It's not fair, but he has to absolve himself of some guilt or it's going to eat him alive.

"Oh, hello!" Hyacine greets, breathless, emerging from the back. "Sorry for the wait, there was a chimera I had to wrangle, they're a lot faster than you'd imagine... What brings you two here?"

"Lord Phainon has a question for you," Castoric says, before he can speak for himself.

Damnit. He swears he sees Hyacine's eyelid twitch.

"It's a normal question," he explains, hoping it'll convince her.

"You can ask me any questions you wish, normal or not. It's my job as your physician."

It's not about whether he can but if he should, but that's not pertinent, he hopes. As he explains his current inability to think about anything other than Mydei and his wellbeing, she relaxes, and gives him an encouraging smile whenever he falters. He still finds it a bit embarrassing.

"I feel like I'm going through puberty again with all these crazy instincts I can't control, but it's worse, somehow...y'know?" he finishes lamely.

Hyacine, at least, does know. "Considering how intensely Mydei's pheromones have affected you in the past, I'm not surprised to hear this. Your own hormones are very sensitive to external influence. Most alphas experience an increase in protective instincts brought on by the chemical change in their mate's scent, even if they can't consciously detect them, and you're just experiencing a more extreme version of that."

"So, I'll go back to normal when the baby's born?" he asks, momentarily relieved, until Hyacine shakes her head.

"It will probably take a few months, since Mydei's scent will take a while to return to its baseline, and the baby will also affect you. A parental bond forms in the first week or so of life, and they will rely on smell and sound to recognize you, as newborns have very poor eyesight. Your body recognizes this, and your scent will greatly increase in strength. This inevitably causes side effects, similar to the ones you're already experiencing."

"But how am I supposed to parent when I can't think clearly?"

"If these feelings are genuinely disruptive, there is a medicine I have that could help... It's for those who overexpress secondary sex hormones, but it doesn't always work."

Are his instincts truly disruptive? If he's being honest with himself, they aren't. He just doesn't appreciate the loss of control over something that he once managed without issue. And maybe that's worth examining, but it's a lot easier to pick this solution, and he doesn't really have the bandwidth for introspection.

"Let me try it, I mean, what's the worst it can do?"

"It doesn't have many side effects, though it can cause drowsiness and muscle aches. You should probably tolerate it well, but please tell me if it doesn't work, and I'll try to figure something else out."

With a bottle of pills in hand, they leave the clinic. Castorice seems rather pleased with herself. Maybe it was her plan all along to get him to come here; she can be awfully conniving when she puts her mind to it. Or maybe he shouldn't question it, and should just appreciate the benefits of her wisdom.

"I guess I should go home to take these," he says, while inspecting the bottle. "Thanks for coming with me."

"It's always a pleasure to spend time with you. I'm going to see Mydei tomorrow to do some more knitting, would you like to join us?"

"Uh... I think I'll pass, Mydei could use some time away from me," he mutters, unwilling to admit that he'd rather not attempt to knit ever again.

"If you're certain. Just make sure you get time to relax and unwind. You won't have as much time for yourself once the baby comes along."

"I'd ought to make the most of this month. I'll go to the baths after this, that should... Hold on, I think I'm getting a call..."

He pulls his teleslate out of his pocket to see it's Mydei, and he swears he can feel the blood drain from his face. He doesn't think Mydei has ever called him before, he only texts. Is Phainon overreacting? He might be, but his hands are already shaking when accepts the call.

"Phainon, where are you?" Mydei asks, tone indistinct and unreadable through the speaker. At least he's alive, Phainon thinks, and tries to feel relieved, but he knows something's wrong.

"Uh, I'm out with Castorice, I told you before I left," he replies. His voice sounds about an octave higher than usual in his ears and he doesn't even care if he's embarrassing himself. If the people walking by see their Deliverer having a breakdown in the middle of the road, they can think whatever they want.

"You should come back to our chambers, I-I... uh..." he stammers, and shit, Phainon doesn't think he's ever heard him stammer before either.

"What's wrong?"

"I believe I'm in labor?"

"What."

Something rustles. "I don't think I pissed myself, there... appears to be a lot of blood--"

"Your water broke? Actually?" His voice, somehow, goes higher. Castorice gasps. The sound seems to come from a thousand miles away.

"Yes, it did--" he says, sounding more certain this time, but it doesn't really matter, because suddenly, everything goes dark.

It feels like a prolonged blink--he's standing in the street one instant, and the next, he's on the ground, and Hyacine and Castorice are both leaning over him. His teleslate is still in his hand, but Hyacine takes it from him and he doesn't try to stop her.

"... passed out, he's... I'll be there..." she says into it, though he can't hear past the ringing in his ears. His head hurts so badly all of a sudden and it's not really making sense.

Mydei's in labor? But he can't be, it's a month early, they were supposed to have another month to prepare. He's not ready, neither of them are ready.

"This is some sort of joke, right?" he mumbles.

"No, Mydei seems quite serious. But how do you feel? I'm guessing the shock made you briefly pass out, which is benign on its own, but you may have injured yourself when you fell."

"My head feels... um... weird."

"Does it hurt?" she asks, already bending down to inspect him.

"It's pounding, but I don't think I hit it?"

"Then that's probably because of the sudden blood pressure change. I don't see any scrapes or wounds, I think you escaped unscathed. Do you think you can stand? I need to go to Mydei, and I'm sure you would like to accompany me."

Oh, right. Phainon feels woozy again, but pushes past it and manages to get up with Hyacine's aid. He can't be fainting right now, there isn't time for that. Mydei's waiting for both of them.

"Is there anything you'd like for me to do?" Castorice pipes up. "I don't think my presence in the delivery room would be safe, but if you wish for me to fetch anyone or anything, I certainly will."

"I need my tools, I didn't grab them on the way out, I was in a rush because of Phainon. Little Ica, can you lead her to the supply room and show her the right bag? I'll give you a treat if you do."

The memosprite immediately perks up at the mention of food, and whizzes from Hyacine's side to Castorice with a happy trill. When it seems certain she's paying attention, it starts off down the road, fast enough for her to have to jog along. Hyacine calls for it to slow down, but to no avail.

"I need a better assistant," she mutters under her breath, before turning to Phainon. "Let's go, time is of the essence."

Unfortunately, Phainon's not very steady on his feet, and it takes all of his focus just to not fall back over. The trip to the Mamoreal Palace seems to take an eon. By the time they actually make it to their chambers, he can't do anything other than stumble over to the desk chair to sit down.

"By Nikador, you actually passed out," Mydei comments. Now that Phainon's vision isn't vignetting, he looks up to find his mate seeming quite relaxed, in contrast to how he sounded on the call. He's laid on the bed with the sheets removed, replaced by a few towels.

"It can't be that obvious," he protests weakly.

"You're paler than the day you accidentally fell into the river outside Okhema and almost drowned. You're not even actively suffocating this time."

"I did not accidentally fall in, I was trying to escape a swarm of harpies, and also--... Okay, we can discuss this later, how are you doing?"

"As well as I can be, considering the circumstances... I'm not sure why I've gone into labor so early, I believed my body was incapable of encountering these kinds of issues."

"I would concur," Hyacine says, "but since this has happened, I would guess that the stress you've endured over the course of your pregnancy, and the injuries you sustained, might've had some effect on you. Try not to worry about it, though. You're late preterm, right on the edge of being unremarkable, so I don't anticipate that there will be any long-term issues with your baby, or short-term, for that matter. I'll be here to take care of anything that does crop up."

Mydei's expression sours, and Phainon already knows what he's thinking. He feels the same way, though he's blaming himself instead. It was his lack of willingness to communicate that led to Mydei putting himself through all that stress--

But no, now's certainly not the time to play this game.

"Neither of us can change the past," he says, because they both know it's true, even though he thinks they've both failed to internalize it. Maybe if he repeats it enough times, they'll finally stop trying to blame themselves for things that don't matter anymore.

Mydei doesn't say anything. He sighs heavily before motioning for Phainon to join him on the bed, which he does immediately, dizziness forgotten. They didn't get a chance to fully discuss how Mydei wanted this to go, so he'll just do whatever is asked of him. That's the important part, right?

The labor is long. Phainon wishes it wasn't, for Mydei's sake and his own. The minutes crawl by in agonizing silence. Mydei doesn't speak much at all, and doesn't make any sound, either, despite the pain he must be in. He just lays on his side, eyes closed, breathing steadily, for the rest of the day.

Phainon doesn't know what to do with himself. He wants to be helpful, but Mydei doesn't ask anything of him, so he just sits there and watches him bleed. Titans, there's so much blood. They've already had to replace the towels a few times and the freshest set is already stained gold. Hyacine was concerned initially, but after confirming the baby wasn't in distress, determined it was alright. Mydei's body can easily handle this level of blood loss, but that doesn't mean Phainon likes watching it.

"Premature births are quite unpredictable," she says, perhaps hoping to make him feel better. He's not really sure if it does. He feels like he's wading through molasses with each step he paces across the room. With Kephale's light perpetually shining, it's easy to lose track of time, and Phainon no longer cares to know the hour.

He doesn't quite return to reality when labor progresses. Sitting next to Mydei, letting him squeeze his hand until the bones feel like they're going to shatter, he can almost believe he's dreaming. It's happening now, and he's still not ready. He wasn't going to be ready even if the baby wasn't pre-term, but he wanted more time.

"Take this baby out of me right now," Mydei hisses under his breath. A part of Phainon agrees, and a part of him wants to run away. He doesn't, of course. He sits and lets Mydei break his hand and finds himself following along to Hyacine's breathing instructions.

And then Mydei makes a final, strangled sound of exertion, and then there's crying, and then Hyacine's wiping the ichor off of a beautiful baby girl with a relieved smile on her face.

Their daughter looks impossibly small rested against Mydei's chest. Phainon can't see her very well past the tears in his eyes. He tries to say something but it comes out as a garbled mess instead, and maybe that expresses his feelings well enough.

Hyacine says something about her body temperature being a bit low as she rests a blanket over her. Phainon only kind of listens. He can't stop staring at his daughter, his and Mydei's daughter. How did he contribute to making such a perfect little thing?

"Phainon, you should hold her too," Mydei insists, and all of a sudden, he finds her bundled up in his arms.

She's so small. He must've said that out loud, because Hyacine assures him her birth weight is very close to normal, and she'll catch up quickly. But that doesn't change her in this moment, and Phainon worries about how fragile she looks. He doesn't want to put her down, though. She seems so comfortable nestled against him and--and gods, when she opens her bleary eyes, they're blue, just like his own.

"Hi there," he manages to choke out. He's smiling so wide his cheeks are starting to hurt.

"I want to name her Anemone," Mydei says softly, "I know we didn't get to discuss it much, but... I like that name."

Phainon nods vigorously, not sure if he can speak anymore than he just did.

Anemone. It's perfect. He's going to do all he can to be the best father for her, she deserves everything he can give.

Three years later, Anemone is old enough to run confidently around the Mamoreal Palace under Aglaea's watch, her still-clumsy fingers can put together crafts with Castorice's guidance, and she can speak in sentences clear enough for her new friends at daycare to understand her. Mydei and Phainon have long since returned to their regular duties, and she loves to hear the stories of all their heroic battles, of course watered down to be appropriate for a young child.

Her blood runs gold, just like theirs. She wants to be a hero too, she proclaims, while swinging around sticks with reckless abandon, though she also wants to be an artist, a doctor, a seamstress, and a hundred other things. They encourage her to follow her heart. Neither of them want her to be forced down the same path they were. Her future should be free of the burden of the Flamechase.

But life is comfortable, even if it's not always peaceful. Neither of them would have it any other way.

And then, two outlanders arrive in Okhema.
